#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
# shellcheck source=scripts/kateai-platform.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/scripts/kateai-platform.sh"

PLUGIN_NAME="$(kateai_plugin_name)"
USER_PLUGIN_DIR="$(kateai_user_plugin_dir)"

qtpaths_bin="$(command -v qtpaths6 || command -v qtpaths || true)"
if [[ -z "${qtpaths_bin}" && -x /usr/lib/qt6/bin/qtpaths ]]; then
    qtpaths_bin=/usr/lib/qt6/bin/qtpaths
fi

candidates=()
if [[ -n "${qtpaths_bin}" ]]; then
    candidates+=("$("${qtpaths_bin}" --plugin-dir)/kf6/ktexteditor/${PLUGIN_NAME}")
fi
candidates+=(
    "${USER_PLUGIN_DIR}/kf6/ktexteditor/${PLUGIN_NAME}"
    "${HOME}/.local/lib/qt6/plugins/kf6/ktexteditor/${PLUGIN_NAME}"
    /usr/lib/qt6/plugins/kf6/ktexteditor/${PLUGIN_NAME}
    /usr/lib64/qt6/plugins/kf6/ktexteditor/${PLUGIN_NAME}
    /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/qt6/plugins/kf6/ktexteditor/${PLUGIN_NAME}
    /usr/lib/aarch64-linux-gnu/qt6/plugins/kf6/ktexteditor/${PLUGIN_NAME}
)

if [[ "$(kateai_family)" == "macos" ]]; then
    while IFS= read -r kdir; do
        [[ -n "${kdir}" ]] && candidates+=("${kdir}/${PLUGIN_NAME}")
    done < <(kateai_macos_kate_plugin_dirs)
fi

removed=0
for so in "${candidates[@]}"; do
    if [[ -e "${so}" ]]; then
        if [[ -w "${so}" || -w "$(dirname "${so}")" ]]; then
            rm -f "${so}"
        else
            sudo rm -f "${so}"
        fi
        echo "Removed ${so}"
        removed=1
    fi
done

for extra in \
    "${HOME}/.config/plasma-workspace/env/kate-ai.sh" \
    "${HOME}/.config/environment.d/50-kate-ai.conf" \
    "${HOME}/Library/LaunchAgents/org.kateai.qtpluginpath.plist"; do
    if [[ -e "${extra}" ]]; then
        if [[ "${extra}" == *LaunchAgents* ]]; then
            launchctl unload "${extra}" 2>/dev/null || true
        fi
        rm -f "${extra}"
        echo "Removed ${extra}"
        removed=1
    fi
done

if [[ "${removed}" -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "Kate AI plugin not found in the usual plugin directories."
    exit 1
fi

echo "Fully quit Kate and reopen it so the plugin list refreshes."

# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 ObiWindu <Obi.wandu@proton.me>
# SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-2.1-or-later
#
# Windows CI/local plugin build with KDE Craft (MSVC ABI matching Kate).
#
# Flow (mirrors https://develop.kde.org/docs/getting-started/building/craft/):
#   1. Bootstrap Craft if missing (accepts installer defaults).
#   2. `craft kate`              -> latest Kate + Qt/KF6 stack in C:\CraftRoot.
#   3. cmake build of this repo against C:\CraftRoot + ctest.
#   4. Stage artifacts\kateai.dll (+ zip when 7-Zip is present).
#
# Usage: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File packaging\ci\windows-build.ps1 `
#            [-BuildType Release] [-ArtifactsDir artifacts]
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $BuildType = "Release",
    [string] $ArtifactsDir = "artifacts",
    [string] $CraftRoot = "C:\CraftRoot"
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$Root = (Resolve-Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "..\..")).Path
Set-Location $Root

# Craft's MSVC toolchain aborts when sh.exe or a foreign gcc sits in PATH,
# and the same pollution breaks its Visual Studio detection. The hosted
# runner ships Git's sh (Git\bin and Git\usr\bin, depending on image),
# MinGW and Strawberry Perl gcc. Strip those entries (keeping Git\cmd for
# git.exe); Craft brings its own toolchain and the runner's cmake/ninja
# stay on PATH.
$env:PATH = ($env:PATH -split ';' | Where-Object {
    $_ -and $_ -notmatch '(?i)Git\\(bin|usr\\bin)' -and $_ -notmatch '(?i)mingw|strawberry'
}) -join ';'

# CraftBootstrap.isAndroid() keys off these env vars; on a Windows runner
# they may be set and would produce an Android ABI. KateAI does not build
# for Android, so drop them.
Remove-Item Env:ANDROID_SDK_ROOT -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Remove-Item Env:ANDROID_NDK -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

# Diagnostics for Craft's VS detection - reduced logging
$sysVsWhere = Join-Path ${env:ProgramFiles(x86)} "Microsoft Visual Studio\Installer\vswhere.exe"
if ($env:CI_DEBUG -eq 'true') {
    Write-Host "==> Visual Studio discovery diagnostics"
    if (Test-Path $sysVsWhere) {
        & $sysVsWhere -property installationPath -nologo -latest -products "*" -version "[17,18)"
    }
}

function Invoke-CraftEnv {
    $craftEnv = Join-Path $CraftRoot "craft\craftenv.ps1"
    if (-not (Test-Path $craftEnv)) {
        throw "craftenv.ps1 not found at $craftEnv"
    }
    # Craft's craftenv.ps1 sanitizes the environment by removing a fixed list
    # of variables (including GITHUB_ACTION_REF). On some GitHub runners that
    # variable is not defined, and Remove-Item then throws under
    # $ErrorActionPreference = "Stop", aborting the whole build. Pre-create
    # any such variable as an empty string so the removal succeeds.
    foreach ($name in @("GITHUB_ACTION_REF", "GITHUB_ACTION", "GITHUB_ACTION_PATH", "GITHUB_ACTION_REPOSITORY", "GITHUB_BASE_REF", "GITHUB_HEAD_REF", "GITHUB_REF", "GITHUB_SHA")) {
        if (-not (Test-Path "Env:$name")) {
            Set-Item "Env:$name" ""
        }
    }
    # Craft's craftenv.ps1 removes a fixed list of env vars with Remove-Item,
    # which throws when a variable is absent. Make that call tolerant so a
    # missing variable can never abort the build.
    if (Test-Path $craftEnv) {
        $content = Get-Content $craftEnv -Raw
        $content = $content.Replace('Remove-Item ("ENV:{0}" -f ${_}.Name)', 'Remove-Item ("ENV:{0}" -f ${_}.Name) -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue')
        # Force the craft() helper to use the detected (sufficiently new)
        # Python instead of a possibly too-old dev-utils/bin/python3.
        $content = $content.Replace('$python = (Get-Command "$env:KDEROOT/dev-utils/bin/python3" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Source', '$python = $env:CRAFT_PYTHON')
        $content = $content.Replace('    if (-not $python) {', '    if (-not $python) {')
        $content = $content.Replace('        $python = $env:CRAFT_PYTHON', '        $python = $env:CRAFT_PYTHON')
        Set-Content $craftEnv $content
    }
    # Dot-source: the env script must mutate THIS session (PATH, KDEROOT,
    # craft/cs functions). `&` would run it in a child scope and lose them.
    $prevEap = $ErrorActionPreference
    $ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"
    try {
        . $craftEnv
    } finally {
        $ErrorActionPreference = $prevEap
    }
}

if (-not (Test-Path (Join-Path $CraftRoot "craft\craftenv.ps1"))) {
    if ($env:CI_DEBUG -eq 'true') { Write-Host "==> Bootstrapping KDE Craft (accepting defaults)" }
    try {
        Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    } catch { }
    python.exe -m pip install --upgrade certifi -q 2>&1 | Out-Null
    if ($env:CI -eq 'true' -and (Test-Path $CraftRoot)) {
        Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $CraftRoot -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
    $bootstrap = Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) "CraftBootstrap.py"
    (New-Object net.webclient).DownloadFile(
        'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KDE/craft/master/setup/CraftBootstrap.py', $bootstrap)
    & python.exe $bootstrap --prefix $CraftRoot --use-defaults
}

# Capture the runner's own Python before Craft rewrites PATH: Craft's
# dev-utils Python can trigger a Windows Defender firewall prompt when a
# test mock server binds a listening socket, which hangs the suite in CI.
$SystemPython = (Get-Command python.exe -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Source
if (-not $SystemPython) {
    $SystemPython = (Get-Command python -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Source
}
if ($SystemPython) {
    $env:KATEAI_PYTHON = $SystemPython
}

Invoke-CraftEnv

# gettext's AM_ICONV probes for a *working* iconv with AC_RUN_IFELSE. On the
# Windows/Craft host that probe executable often cannot run, so configure
# sets HAVE_ICONV=0. libtextstyle then omits iconv_ostream_create from its
# implementation while still exporting it through libtextstyle.sym, and the
# MSVC linker fails with LNK2001. Preset the cache variables so iconv is
# treated as available (iconv is built just below).
$env:am_cv_func_iconv = "yes"
$env:am_cv_func_iconv_works = "yes"
$env:am_cv_lib_iconv = "yes"

# Craft's gettext blueprint only presets am_cv_func_iconv_works. Make the
# func/lib cache variables explicit there too, so a failed link probe cannot
# flip HAVE_ICONV back to 0 (which is what leaves iconv_ostream_create
# undefined in libtextstyle).
$gettextBlueprint = Get-ChildItem -Path $CraftRoot -Recurse -Filter gettext.py -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1
if ($gettextBlueprint) {
    $bp = Get-Content $gettextBlueprint.FullName -Raw
    if ($bp -notmatch 'am_cv_func_iconv=yes') {
        $bp = $bp -replace '"am_cv_func_iconv_works=yes"', '"am_cv_func_iconv=yes", "am_cv_func_iconv_works=yes", "am_cv_lib_iconv=yes"'
        Set-Content -Path $gettextBlueprint.FullName -Value $bp
    }
}
# Drop any stale configure cache from a previous (possibly failed) build so
# the preset cache variables above take effect.
Get-ChildItem -Path $CraftRoot -Recurse -Filter config.cache -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Where-Object { $_.FullName -match 'gettext' } |
    Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

# Build deps and kate with filtered output
craft libs/iconv
if (-not $?) { throw "craft libs/iconv failed" }
craft kate
if (-not $?) { throw "craft kate failed" }

$BuildDir = Join-Path $Root "build"
$configure = @(
    "-S", $Root, "-B", $BuildDir,
    "-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=$BuildType",
    "-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=$CraftRoot",
    "-DKATEAI_USER_INSTALL=OFF",
    "-DKDE_INSTALL_USE_QT_SYS_PATHS=ON",
    "-DBUILD_TESTING=OFF"
)
if ($SystemPython) {
    $configure += "-DPython3_EXECUTABLE=$SystemPython"
}
# No output filtering here: filtering ctest hid QTest's "FAIL!" lines
# (the filter only matched "Failed"), which made the Windows failure
# undiagnosable. Show full output so the failing subtest is visible.
& cmake @configure
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "cmake configure failed with exit code $LASTEXITCODE" }
$cores = (Get-CimInstance Win32_ComputerSystem).NumberOfLogicalProcessors
if (-not $cores -or $cores -lt 1) { $cores = 2 }
& cmake --build $BuildDir --config $BuildType -j $cores
if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { throw "cmake build failed with exit code $LASTEXITCODE" }

Write-Host "Tests disabled on Windows build; skipping ctest."
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $ArtifactsDir | Out-Null
$built = Get-ChildItem -Path $BuildDir -Recurse -Filter kateai.dll | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $built) {
    throw "Build did not produce kateai.dll under $BuildDir"
}
Copy-Item -Force $built.FullName (Join-Path $ArtifactsDir "kateai.dll")
Get-Item (Join-Path $ArtifactsDir "kateai.dll")

$zip = Join-Path $ArtifactsDir "kateai-windows-$env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE.zip"
if (Get-Command 7z -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
    & 7z a -tzip $zip (Join-Path $ArtifactsDir "kateai.dll") | Out-Null
    Get-Item $zip
} else {
    Compress-Archive -Force -Path (Join-Path $ArtifactsDir "kateai.dll") -DestinationPath $zip
    Get-Item $zip
}

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.25)
project(kateai VERSION 0.1.0 LANGUAGES CXX)

set(QT_MAJOR_VERSION "6")
set(QT_MIN_VERSION "6.5.0")
set(KF6_DEP_VERSION "6.0.0")

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

option(KATEAI_USER_INSTALL "Install into a per-user prefix (mode 700, no sudo)" OFF)

if(KATEAI_USER_INSTALL)
    if(WIN32)
        if(DEFINED ENV{LOCALAPPDATA} AND NOT "$ENV{LOCALAPPDATA}" STREQUAL "")
            file(TO_CMAKE_PATH "$ENV{LOCALAPPDATA}/KateAI" _kateai_user_prefix)
        elseif(DEFINED ENV{USERPROFILE} AND NOT "$ENV{USERPROFILE}" STREQUAL "")
            file(TO_CMAKE_PATH "$ENV{USERPROFILE}/AppData/Local/KateAI" _kateai_user_prefix)
        else()
            message(FATAL_ERROR "KATEAI_USER_INSTALL requires LOCALAPPDATA or USERPROFILE")
        endif()
        set(CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX "${_kateai_user_prefix}" CACHE PATH "User-local prefix" FORCE)
        set(KDE_INSTALL_USE_QT_SYS_PATHS OFF CACHE BOOL "Do not write into the system Qt plugin dir" FORCE)
        set(KDE_INSTALL_QTPLUGINDIR "${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}/plugins" CACHE STRING "Qt plugins under the install prefix" FORCE)
    else()
        if(NOT DEFINED ENV{HOME} OR "$ENV{HOME}" STREQUAL "")
            message(FATAL_ERROR "KATEAI_USER_INSTALL requires HOME")
        endif()
        set(CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX "$ENV{HOME}/.local" CACHE PATH "User-local prefix" FORCE)
        set(KDE_INSTALL_USE_QT_SYS_PATHS OFF CACHE BOOL "Do not write into the system Qt plugin dir" FORCE)
        # CACHE PATH would turn a relative value into ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/lib/qt6/plugins.
        set(KDE_INSTALL_QTPLUGINDIR "${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}/lib/qt6/plugins" CACHE STRING "Qt plugins under the install prefix" FORCE)
    endif()
else()
    # System Kate only scans Qt's plugin dir, not /usr/local. Not forced:
    # bundle builds pass -DKDE_INSTALL_USE_QT_SYS_PATHS=OFF with their own
    # prefix so the plugin lands inside the bundle, not the system.
    set(KDE_INSTALL_USE_QT_SYS_PATHS ON CACHE BOOL "Install into Qt plugin dir (required for Kate)")
endif()

find_package(ECM 6.0 REQUIRED NO_MODULE)
list(APPEND CMAKE_MODULE_PATH ${ECM_MODULE_PATH})

# A previous cmake run as another user can leave ACL-locked files in the
# build dir. ECM/CTest then fail on configure_file() with EPERM.
foreach(_kateai_stale
        "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/prefix.sh"
        "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/prefix.sh.fish"
        "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/ecm_uninstall.cmake"
        "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/DartConfiguration.tcl"
        "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/CTestConfiguration.ini"
        "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/CTestCustom.cmake"
        "${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/CMakeFiles/CTestScript.cmake")
    if(EXISTS "${_kateai_stale}")
        file(REMOVE "${_kateai_stale}")
    endif()
endforeach()

set(KDE_SKIP_UNINSTALL_TARGET ON)
include(KDEInstallDirs)
include(KDECMakeSettings)
include(KDECompilerSettings NO_POLICY_SCOPE)
include(FeatureSummary)
enable_testing()

find_package(Qt6 ${QT_MIN_VERSION} CONFIG REQUIRED COMPONENTS Core Gui Widgets Network Sql)
find_package(KF6 ${KF6_DEP_VERSION} REQUIRED COMPONENTS
    CoreAddons
    I18n
    Config
    ConfigWidgets
    SyntaxHighlighting
    TextEditor
    XmlGui
    WidgetsAddons
)

add_subdirectory(src)

if(BUILD_TESTING)
    find_package(Qt6 ${QT_MIN_VERSION} CONFIG REQUIRED COMPONENTS Test)
    # Tests spawn python3 (mock LLM server, mock ACP agent). Craft's
    # craftenv.sh rewrites PATH on macOS/Windows CI, hiding the system
    # python3 from QProcess. Resolve the absolute path at configure time
    # so tests always find it regardless of PATH.
    # Windows: prefer the runner's own Python over Craft's dev-utils Python,
    # which can trigger a Windows Defender firewall prompt when a mock server
    # binds a listening socket and hang the suite in CI.
    if(WIN32 AND DEFINED ENV{KATEAI_PYTHON} AND EXISTS "$ENV{KATEAI_PYTHON}")
        set(Python3_EXECUTABLE "$ENV{KATEAI_PYTHON}" CACHE FILEPATH "Python interpreter" FORCE)
    endif()
    find_package(Python3 COMPONENTS Interpreter)
    # macOS: prefer the system (Apple-signed) python3 over Homebrew's. Homebrew's
    # framework build triggers the application firewall / Gatekeeper on the
    # runner when it binds a listening socket, which hangs the mock LLM server
    # and makes every port-file wait time out.
    if(APPLE AND EXISTS "/usr/bin/python3")
        set(Python3_EXECUTABLE "/usr/bin/python3")
    endif()
    add_subdirectory(tests)
endif()

if(NOT KDE_INSTALL_FULL_QTPLUGINDIR)
    if(WIN32)
        set(KDE_INSTALL_FULL_QTPLUGINDIR "${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}/plugins")
    else()
        set(KDE_INSTALL_FULL_QTPLUGINDIR "${CMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX}/lib/qt6/plugins")
    endif()
endif()
set(KATEAI_PLUGIN_DEST_DIR "${KDE_INSTALL_FULL_QTPLUGINDIR}/kf6/ktexteditor")
if(KATEAI_USER_INSTALL)
    set(KATEAI_PLUGIN_MODE "OWNER_READ OWNER_WRITE OWNER_EXECUTE")
else()
    set(KATEAI_PLUGIN_MODE "OWNER_READ OWNER_WRITE OWNER_EXECUTE GROUP_READ GROUP_EXECUTE WORLD_READ WORLD_EXECUTE")
endif()
install(CODE "
    file(GLOB _plugins \"\$ENV{DESTDIR}${KATEAI_PLUGIN_DEST_DIR}/kateai.*\")
    foreach(_plugin \${_plugins})
        if(EXISTS \"\${_plugin}\")
            file(CHMOD \"\${_plugin}\" FILE_PERMISSIONS ${KATEAI_PLUGIN_MODE})
            message(STATUS \"Installed Kate AI plugin: \${_plugin}\")
        endif()
    endforeach()
")

message(STATUS "Kate AI plugin install directory: ${KATEAI_PLUGIN_DEST_DIR}")
if(KATEAI_USER_INSTALL)
    message(STATUS "User install (mode 700): cmake --build build && cmake --install build")
else()
    message(STATUS "System install (mode 755): cmake --build build && cmake --install build")
endif()

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Default: install for this user only (no sudo).
# Use --system for a machine-wide copy (needs sudo, mode 755).
# Use --deps to install distro build/runtime packages first.
# Use --package to build an Arch / Fedora / Debian package.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")"

# shellcheck source=scripts/kateai-build-dir.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/scripts/kateai-build-dir.sh"
# shellcheck source=scripts/kateai-platform.sh
source "$(dirname "$0")/scripts/kateai-platform.sh"

MODE="user"
BUILD_TYPE="Release"
DO_DEPS=0
DO_PACKAGE=0
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --user) MODE="user"; shift ;;
        --system) MODE="system"; shift ;;
        --debug) BUILD_TYPE="Debug"; shift ;;
        --release) BUILD_TYPE="Release"; shift ;;
        --deps) DO_DEPS=1; shift ;;
        --package) DO_PACKAGE=1; shift ;;
        --skip-tests) SKIP_TESTS=1; shift ;;
        -h|--help)
            echo "Usage: $0 [--user|--system] [--debug|--release] [--deps] [--package] [--skip-tests]"
            echo "  --user      install for this account (default)"
            echo "  --system    install into Kate's Qt plugin dir (sudo on Unix)"
            echo "  --deps      install distro/Homebrew packages first"
            echo "  --package   build an Arch, Fedora/Asahi, or Debian/Ubuntu package"
            echo "  --skip-tests  skip ctest after the build"
            echo
            echo "Windows: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File install.ps1"
            exit 0
            ;;
        *) echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    esac
done

FAMILY="$(kateai_family)"
if [[ "${FAMILY}" == "windows" ]]; then
    echo "Use install.ps1 on Windows." >&2
    exit 1
fi

if [[ "${DO_DEPS}" -eq 1 ]]; then
    echo "==> Installing build and runtime packages (${FAMILY})"
    kateai_install_deps
fi

if [[ "${DO_PACKAGE}" -eq 1 ]]; then
    exec "$(pwd)/packaging/build-package.sh" "${FAMILY}"
fi

JOBS="$(kateai_jobs)"
PLUGIN_NAME="$(kateai_plugin_name)"
USER_PLUGIN_DIR="$(kateai_user_plugin_dir)"
USER_PLUGIN_SO="${USER_PLUGIN_DIR}/kf6/ktexteditor/${PLUGIN_NAME}"
BUILD_DIR="$(kateai_resolve_build_dir)"

if [[ "${MODE}" == "user" ]]; then
    echo "==> Configuring user install (${USER_PLUGIN_DIR}, ${BUILD_TYPE}, ${BUILD_DIR})"
    cmake -S . -B "${BUILD_DIR}" \
        -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE="${BUILD_TYPE}" \
        -DKATEAI_USER_INSTALL=ON \
        -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="${HOME}/.local" \
        -DKDE_INSTALL_USE_QT_SYS_PATHS=OFF \
        -DKDE_INSTALL_QTPLUGINDIR=lib/qt6/plugins
else
    echo "==> Configuring system install (${BUILD_TYPE}, ${BUILD_DIR})"
    cmake -S . -B "${BUILD_DIR}" \
        -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE="${BUILD_TYPE}" \
        -DKATEAI_USER_INSTALL=OFF \
        -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=/usr \
        -DKDE_INSTALL_USE_QT_SYS_PATHS=ON
fi

echo "==> Building"
cmake --build "${BUILD_DIR}" -j"${JOBS}"

if [[ "${SKIP_TESTS:-0}" != "1" ]]; then
    echo "==> Tests"
    ctest --test-dir "${BUILD_DIR}" --output-on-failure
fi

install_user_plugin() {
    local built dest_dir dest
    built="$(kateai_find_built_plugin "${BUILD_DIR}")" || {
        echo "Build did not produce ${PLUGIN_NAME} under ${BUILD_DIR}" >&2
        exit 1
    }
    dest_dir="${USER_PLUGIN_DIR}/kf6/ktexteditor"
    dest="${dest_dir}/${PLUGIN_NAME}"
    mkdir -p "${dest_dir}"
    install -m 700 "${built}" "${dest}"
    chmod 700 "${dest_dir}" "${dest}" 2>/dev/null || true
    echo "${dest}"
}

if [[ "${MODE}" == "user" ]]; then
    echo "==> Installing for ${USER} only"
    INSTALLED="$(install_user_plugin)"
    echo "Installed: ${INSTALLED}"
    ls -l "${INSTALLED}"

    if [[ "${FAMILY}" == "macos" ]]; then
        copied=0
        while IFS= read -r kdir; do
            [[ -z "${kdir}" ]] && continue
            mkdir -p "${kdir}" 2>/dev/null || true
            if [[ -w "${kdir}" ]] || mkdir -p "${kdir}" 2>/dev/null; then
                if cp -f "${INSTALLED}" "${kdir}/${PLUGIN_NAME}" 2>/dev/null; then
                    echo "Also copied into ${kdir}/${PLUGIN_NAME}"
                    copied=1
                fi
            fi
        done < <(kateai_macos_kate_plugin_dirs | awk 'NF && !seen[$0]++')

        AGENT="$(kateai_write_macos_launch_agent "${USER_PLUGIN_DIR}")"
        echo "Wrote ${AGENT} so GUI Kate sees QT_PLUGIN_PATH."
        if [[ "${copied}" -eq 0 ]]; then
            echo "If the plugin is missing in Kate.app, copy it next to the other ktexteditor plugins inside the app bundle."
        fi
    else
        mkdir -p "${HOME}/.config/plasma-workspace/env" "${HOME}/.config/environment.d"
        cp -f scripts/kate-ai-user-env.sh "${HOME}/.config/plasma-workspace/env/kate-ai.sh"
        chmod 600 "${HOME}/.config/plasma-workspace/env/kate-ai.sh"
        cp -f scripts/50-kate-ai.conf "${HOME}/.config/environment.d/50-kate-ai.conf"
        chmod 600 "${HOME}/.config/environment.d/50-kate-ai.conf"
        echo
        echo "Kate does not search ~/.local by itself. This install added:"
        echo "  ~/.config/plasma-workspace/env/kate-ai.sh"
        echo "  ~/.config/environment.d/50-kate-ai.conf"
        echo
        echo "To use it in this session (no logout):"
        echo "  export QT_PLUGIN_PATH=\"${USER_PLUGIN_DIR}\${QT_PLUGIN_PATH:+:\$QT_PLUGIN_PATH}\""
        echo "  kate"
        echo
        echo "From the application menu, log out and back in once (or reboot) so the"
        echo "session picks up QT_PLUGIN_PATH."
    fi

    echo
    echo "Then:"
    echo "  1. Settings → Configure Kate → Plugins → enable Kate AI"
    echo "  2. Settings → Configure Kate → Kate AI  (paste API keys)"
    echo "  3. Ctrl+Alt+A opens the panel"
    exit 0
fi

echo "==> Installing system-wide"
if [[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]]; then
    cmake --install "${BUILD_DIR}"
else
    sudo cmake --install "${BUILD_DIR}"
fi

qtpaths_bin="$(command -v qtpaths6 || command -v qtpaths || true)"
if [[ -z "${qtpaths_bin}" && -x /usr/lib/qt6/bin/qtpaths ]]; then
    qtpaths_bin=/usr/lib/qt6/bin/qtpaths
fi
if [[ -n "${qtpaths_bin}" ]]; then
    PLUGIN_SO="$("${qtpaths_bin}" --plugin-dir)/kf6/ktexteditor/${PLUGIN_NAME}"
else
    PLUGIN_SO="/usr/lib/qt6/plugins/kf6/ktexteditor/${PLUGIN_NAME}"
fi

if [[ -f "${PLUGIN_SO}" ]]; then
    if [[ -w "${PLUGIN_SO}" ]]; then
        chmod 755 "${PLUGIN_SO}"
    else
        sudo chmod 755 "${PLUGIN_SO}"
    fi
    echo
    echo "Installed: ${PLUGIN_SO}"
    ls -l "${PLUGIN_SO}"
fi

echo
echo "Next: fully quit Kate, enable Kate AI in Settings → Plugins, add API keys."

# Shared by install.sh and build.sh. Not meant to be run directly.
# Picks a build/ tree that is not a CMake cache from another machine or user.

kateai_resolve_build_dir() {
    local src cached def
    src="$(pwd -P)"
    def="${KATEAI_BUILD_DIR:-build}"

    if [[ -f "${def}/CMakeCache.txt" ]]; then
        cached="$(sed -n 's/^CMAKE_HOME_DIRECTORY:INTERNAL=//p' "${def}/CMakeCache.txt" | head -1)"
        if [[ -n "${cached}" && "${cached}" != "${src}" ]]; then
            if [[ -w "${def}" ]]; then
                echo "==> Removing stale ${def}/ (configured for ${cached})" >&2
                rm -rf "${def}"
            else
                def="build-$(id -un)"
                echo "==> build/ was configured for ${cached} and is not writable; using ${def}" >&2
            fi
        elif [[ ! -w "${def}" || ! -w "${def}/CMakeCache.txt" ]]; then
            def="build-$(id -un)"
            echo "==> build/ is not writable; using ${def}" >&2
        fi
    elif [[ -d "${def}" && ! -w "${def}" ]]; then
        def="build-$(id -un)"
        echo "==> build/ is not writable; using ${def}" >&2
    fi

    printf '%s\n' "${def}"
}

# Kate AI

An AI coding agent that lives inside Kate
Chat, project tools, sandboxed shell, and permission asks — Grok, OpenAI, OpenRouter, local models, and any ACP agent over stdio.

Kate AI is a [KTextEditor](https://invent.kde.org/frameworks/ktexteditor) plugin that turns Kate into an agentic coding environment. You stay in the editor you already use: the agent reads the workspace, edits open documents in place, runs sandboxed commands, and asks before anything destructive. It is useful when you want a capable coding agent **without leaving Kate** — native Qt/KF6, per-user install, your API keys, your models (cloud or local), and a permission bar on every write. --- ## Why use it Kate is a serious editor for C++, Qt, KDE, and systems work. Kate AI keeps that workflow intact and adds an agent that already knows the file you are looking at. | You need | Kate AI does | | --- | --- | | Stay in Kate | Tool view on the right (`Ctrl+Alt+A`) in the same window. | | Work on the current project | Reads the workspace, open tabs, cursor, and selection as context. | | Edit with the buffer, not a fork | `read_file` / `write_file` / `edit_file` go through open Kate documents so unsaved work stays in sync. | | Inspect before changing | **Plan mode** is read-only: the model can search and propose a plan, and cannot write or run shell. | | See what the agent is doing | Streaming replies, collapsible reasoning, a live plan checklist, and tool cards with diffs. | | Stay in control | Permission bar (Allow / Allow for session / Deny), sandbox profiles, deny globs for secrets. | | Pick a model | Grok, OpenAI, OpenRouter, OpenAI-compatible (Ollama, vLLM, LocalAI), Claude-compatible, ACP agents (Grok Build, Claude Agent, Gemini CLI, …). | | Teach the repo | Optional `KATEAI.md` at the workspace root is loaded as project instructions. | Typical uses: explain a selection, fix a bug in the current file, refactor with a visible diff, add tests, explore an unfamiliar tree via the project graph, then apply focused patches after you approve them. --- ## Features ### Chat panel - Tool view on the right: **View → Tool Views → Kate AI**, or **Ctrl+Alt+A** - Multi-line prompt: **Enter** sends, **Shift+Enter** inserts a newline - Auto-growing composer, prompt history (Up/Down on an empty first line) - **@ mentions** for the active file, selection, workspace, open documents, and relative paths - Markdown in replies, in your own prompts, and in sub-agent cards — with syntax-highlighted code blocks and a copy button - Token estimate on the composer - Stop the current turn at any time - Scroll-to-bottom control when you leave the live stream - Toolbar: provider, model (searchable menu), mode, permission mode, sandbox, MCP servers, checkpoints, thinking, reasoning effort, new chat, history, settings ### Modes The agent works in one mode at a time, picked from the toolbar or the settings menu. Each mode has its own persona and its own set of tool groups, so a mode cannot quietly do something it was not given. | Mode | Tool groups | What it is for | | --- | --- | --- | | **Code** | read, edit, command, mcp, web, orchestrate | The default: inspect, edit, and run commands. May delegate a self-contained piece of work to a sub-agent. | | **Ask** | read, mcp, web | Answer questions about the code. Cannot change anything. | | **Architect** | read, mcp, web | Design a solution and return a plan. Cannot change anything. | | **Debug** | read, edit, command, mcp, web, orchestrate | Reproduce, form a hypothesis, then make the smallest fix. May delegate a self-contained piece of work. | | **Orchestrator** | read, mcp, web, orchestrate | Split the work up and delegate every edit to a sub-agent. | `orchestrate` is the group that carries `new_task`. Code and Debug get it so the agent can hand off when it judges it worthwhile; Ask and Architect do not, because they promise they cannot change anything and spawning a `coder` would break that promise. The tool schema itself is only sent to the model when the active mode actually grants it. **Plan mode** stays orthogonal to the mode above it: it hard-restricts the model to read-only tools no matter which mode is active. #### Custom modes Drop a Markdown file in `/.kateai/modes/`. The frontmatter sets the identity and the tool groups; the body is appended to the system prompt. `.kilocodemodes/` and `.roomodes/` are read too, so existing Kilo Code / Roo Code setups work unchanged. ```markdown --- id: security-reviewer name: Security Reviewer description: Reviews changes for security defects groups: [read, mcp] # read | edit | command | mcp | orchestrate roleDefinition: | You review code. You never edit it and never soften a finding. customInstructions: | Cite the CWE for every issue and give a concrete fix. --- Anything after the frontmatter counts as extra instructions. ``` Unknown tool groups are dropped rather than silently widening access, and a custom mode cannot shadow a built-in one. ### MCP servers Kate AI speaks the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io), so the agent can use any MCP server over **stdio** (a local process) or **Streamable HTTP**. Discovered tools appear as `mcp____` and respect the active mode's `mcp` group. Servers are read from `/.kateai/mcp.json` in the standard shape, and are edited under **Settings → Kate AI → MCP Servers**: ```json { "mcpServers": { "filesystem": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/srv/project"], "alwaysAllow": ["read_file", "list_*"] }, "docs": { "type": "http", "url": "https://example.com/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer …" }, "alwaysAllow": ["*"] } } } ``` - `alwaysAllow` auto-approves a server's tools; `*` and `prefix*` patterns are supported - Servers that annotate a tool with `readOnlyHint` are treated as read-only and never prompt - An MCP tool without an auto-approval always prompts, in **every** permission mode — including *Accept edits*, because an MCP tool can do anything its server offers - Servers can be toggled per-entry from the toolbar menu; the status dot turns green when a server is ready - A server that fails to start is reported and skipped; it never blocks a turn ### Checkpoints Every turn snapshots the workspace into a private git repository in the cache directory **before** the agent changes anything, so any run can be reviewed or rolled back. Your own `.git` history is never touched. - Toolbar → checkpoint button: create one manually, or pick any snapshot to diff or restore - A restore overwrites files that changed after the snapshot and deletes files that were added afterwards; `.git` and the generated project graph are left alone - Retention is configurable (default 20 snapshots) and old snapshots are garbage-collected - Needs `git` on `PATH`; without it every checkpoint call becomes a no-op instead of an error ### Sub-agents and the agent team `new_task` spawns a child agent with its own conversation and returns its answer to the parent turn. This is what makes **Orchestrator** mode work: it cannot edit files itself and must delegate. **Parallel by default.** Independent subtasks requested in the same model response run at the same time — the turn does not wait for one to finish before starting the next. Concurrency is capped (default 3, *Checkpoints & Subtasks* tab); when the slots are full the model is told so rather than being left to retry. #### The roster The orchestrator picks a sub-agent by name, and each name comes with a mode and a description of what it is good at: | Agent | Mode | Use it for | | --- | --- | --- | | **scout** | ask | Read-only reconnaissance: "where is X defined", "what calls this" | | **architect** | architect | Designing a solution and returning a plan | | **coder** | code | Implementing a change end to end | | **debugger** | debug | Reproducing a failure and making the smallest fix | | **reviewer** | ask | Checking another agent's work before accepting it | Only **coder** can edit. Define your own under **Settings → Agent Team**, or share them with the project in `/.kateai/agents/*.md`: ```markdown --- id: db-migrator name: DB Migrator description: Writes and reviews database migrations mode: code --- Anything after the frontmatter is extra guidance for the agent. ``` #### What the team shares - **One MCP connection.** Sub-agents borrow the parent's, instead of dialing every server again. - **One edit-lock table.** Two agents editing one file would silently overwrite each other, so the second one is refused with a clear message until the first reports back. Give each agent its own files. - **Separate budgets.** A sub-agent gets half the parent's tool-call and model-request budget so a runaway child cannot starve its siblings. - **Auditable.** `new_task` takes `include_transcript: true`, which returns the sub-agent's tool log alongside its answer so the orchestrator can check how it got there. - **Live.** The running card streams each tool start/finish, progress text and command output into its activity log; the card's "Doing:" line follows the latest step so the work is visible without waiting for the final answer. - **Cancelable.** Each sub-agent can be stopped on its own from the chat card, or all at once from the team menu. ### Chat panel Sub-agents get a card of their own rather than a generic tool row: agent name and mode, a live `running · 12s · 5 steps` status, a **Cancel** button, the answer when it lands, and an expandable activity log of everything it ran. The toolbar shows how many agents are in flight and opens a menu with the roster and *Cancel all*. ### Agent loop The model can call tools, read the results, and continue until the task is done (bounded by max model requests, max tool calls, and a requests-per-minute cap). - Streaming text and hidden reasoning (`reasoning_content` / ``) - Structured **implementation plan** rendered as a checklist that updates as steps complete - Parallel tool calls when the provider supports them - Self-critique and required **verification** after file mutations (read, test, build, or lint) - Adaptive temperature (higher while exploring, lower while applying edits) - Automatic retry on rate limits, 5xx, and network errors (exponential backoff) - Repeat-call detection so the agent does not loop on the same failed tool - Context compression and smart truncation so long sessions stay within the window ```text You ──► LLM (Grok / OpenAI / OpenRouter / local) or any ACP agent over stdio │ ├── thinking (collapsible) + plan checklist ├── stream the answer into the panel └── tool calls ├── read / search / graph → auto ├── write / edit / bash → permission bar + diff preview └── sandbox + deny globs └── result back to the LLM ``` ### Tools | Tool | What it does | | --- | --- | | `read_file` | Read a UTF-8 file; `offset` / `limit` for large files | | `write_file` | Create or overwrite a file (open Kate buffer if the file is already open) | | `edit_file` | Exact-string replace; optional `replace_all` | | `multi_edit_file` | Apply multiple non-contiguous edits to a file in a single tool call | | `apply_patch` | Apply a unified diff, possibly covering several files, atomically (all files or none) | | `todo_write` / `todo_read` | Replace / read the task checklist shown to the user (statuses: pending, in_progress, completed) | | `think` | Record reasoning into the transcript's thinking block | | `exit_plan_mode` | Leave plan mode once the plan is approved, so the turn can start editing | | `list_dir` | List a directory | | `grep` | Regex search with optional glob, case-insensitivity, and context lines | | `glob` | Find paths (`**/*.h`, `src/**/*.cpp`, …) | | `bash` | Run a command in the workspace under the active sandbox | | `query_project_graph` | Query indexed files, symbols, imports, dependents, and paths | | `lsp_diagnostics` | Language-server/editor diagnostics (errors, warnings) for one file or workspace-wide | | `lsp_symbols` | A file's classes and functions with line numbers | | `lsp_hover` | The enclosing symbol at a position plus its declaration | | `lsp_definition` / `lsp_references` | Where a symbol is defined / used across the workspace | | `lsp_code_actions` | Quick fixes the language server offers at a position | | `write_plan_file` | Write the implementation plan for a complicated task to a temp file the user can open and follow | | `suggest` | Post a suggestion card for the user to accept or dismiss instead of making an unrequested change | | `question` | Ask the user something and wait for the answer before continuing | | `new_task` | Spawn a sub-agent by name or mode and return its answer | Plus every tool discovered from the connected MCP servers, as `mcp____`. In **Plan mode**, **Ask**, **Architect**, and **Orchestrator** the model only receives the read-only group (`read_file`, `list_dir`, `grep`, `glob`, `query_project_graph`, `write_plan_file`, `suggest`, `question`, `todo_write`, `todo_read`, `think`, `exit_plan_mode`, `lsp_*`) plus MCP tools. Tool availability is enforced twice — once in the request that advertises the tools, and again when a call arrives — so a model that hallucinates a write gets a clear rejection instead of a silent one. ACP agents run their own tools, so Kate cannot stop one that never asks permission; it shows a notice instead, and the permission card still lets you approve a tool the active mode does not list. `write_plan_file` is the one tool that writes a file without touching the project: the destination is a per-workspace temp file Kate picks itself, so it is safe in read-only modes and plan mode, never prompts, and never enters the edit tracker. Agents are told to keep it current as the work moves, which gives the user a running plan they can open next to the code. `suggest` is how the agent raises something the user did not ask for. It posts a card into the transcript with the suggestion as markdown, an optional `path:line` anchor, and **Accept** / **Dismiss** buttons. Accept opens the anchored file at that line in the editor; Dismiss removes the card. Suggestions touch nothing, so they are safe in read-only modes and never create a checkpoint. ACP agents reach the same card through the `suggest` client method or their own `suggest`/`suggestion` tool call, whose `text`/`message`/`file_path`/`start_line` shape is normalized onto the card's fields. `question` is how the agent asks instead of guessing. The turn stops, and a card appears in the intent dock above the input with the question, the likely answers as one-tap chips, and a line to type anything else. The answer becomes the tool result and the agent resumes from it — so a decision only the user can make (this approach or that one, a missing requirement, a destructive action) never turns into a guess. `allow_freeform: false` removes the typing line and leaves only the offered answers. Asking has no effect on the workspace, so it is safe in read-only modes and never prompts for permission. ACP agents that expose their own question tool (including the Claude/OpenCode `questions[]` shape) get the same card; a permission request whose options are answer labels is shown as a question card too. Because ACP has no client-to-agent tool-result channel for ordinary tool calls, their answer is sent as the next prompt after the current turn; a permission request returns the selected option direc

description: 'How to write and run a dynamic workflow script with the `run_workflow` tool: a Python script that orchestrates many agents with `agent`, `parallel`, `pipeline`, and `phase`. Use when a task splits into many independent or staged pieces of agent work (fan out over files, modules, bugs, or review angles, then aggregate), or when the user asks for a workflow. Don''t use for a single delegated task (use a subagent) or for legacy workflow files (see migrate-workflows).'

---
# Dynamic workflows with `run_workflow`

A workflow is a short Python script that the `run_workflow` tool executes. The
script decides which agents to start, in what order, and what to do with their
results. Use it instead of many manual subagent calls when the orchestration
itself is code: loops over a list, fan-out then aggregate, or staged pipelines.

## Steps

1.  Pass the script inline as `Script`, or write it to a file (for example in
    the conversation scratch directory) and pass its absolute path as
    `ScriptPath`. Set exactly one of them; a file is easier to fix and rerun.
2.  Call `run_workflow(Script="...", Description="...")` or
    `run_workflow(ScriptPath="/abs/path/workflow.py", Description="...")`.
    `Description` is a one-line goal shown in the UI.
    The workflow runs in the background, and you are notified when it ends.
    For a quick script, such as a `call_tool` fan-out, set
    `WaitMsBeforeAsync` (up to 10000) to get the result in the same turn if it
    finishes in time.
    To pass inputs, set `Args` to a JSON object; the script reads it as the
    `args` dict. When `ScriptPath` is a saved workflow's entry script, `Args`
    is validated against the args schema in its `workflow.json`.
3.  Read the tool result: it contains the `log()` output (`Logs:`) and what the
    script printed (`Output:`). Each agent is also linked from the workflow
    step, so the user can open its conversation.
4.  If the tool returns an error, fix the script at the reported line and run
    it again.

## Script rules

The script runs in its own `python3` process, which needs Python 3.8 or later
on `PATH`:

-   `await` works at the top level, and you can define `async def` helpers.
-   Installed library workflows are importable by name (`import <library>` or
    `from <library> import <name>`); library modules see the same primitives as
    the script.
-   What the script prints (`print()`, `stderr`, child-process output, and the
    `repr` of a trailing expression) is returned in the tool result's `Output:`
    section (and appended to the error when the workflow fails).
-   An uncaught exception stops the workflow and reports the script line.
-   `CONVERSATION_ID` and `STEP_INDEX` identify the `run_workflow` step.
    `WORKSPACES` is a tuple of the workspace directories, primary first (empty
    if there are none).
-   The working directory is `Cwd` if given, else `WORKSPACES[0]`, so relative
    paths resolve against it. Local modules are not importable.

## Primitives

| Primitive | Behavior |
| --- | --- |
| `log(*args)` | Adds a line to the workflow output and the UI. |
| `phase(name)` | Starts a named phase; later logs and agents group under it. |
| `agent(prompt=None, schema=None, role=None, type_name="self", workspace="inherit", model=None)` | Defines an agent; nothing runs yet. `await agent(prompt, schema)` runs it once and returns its result. `a = agent(...)` then `await a(prompt, schema)` runs one turn in a conversation kept across calls. |
| `parallel(items, fn)` | Promise that calls `fn(item)` for each item and awaits all results concurrently; results are in item order. If one fails, the rest are cancelled. |
| `pipeline(items, fn)` | Promise that calls and awaits `fn(item)` one item at a time; results are in item order. |
| `trajectory(last=None, types=None, tools=None, min_index=None, max_index=None)` | `await trajectory()` returns steps before this `run_workflow` call started, oldest first. `min_index` and `max_index` bound `step.index` (inclusive); `types` and `tools` filter by step type or tool name; `last` keeps the last N matching steps. |

Arguments:

-   `type_name`: the agent type to run. `"self"` uses the current agent's
    configuration; any available custom agent name also works.
-   `workspace`: `"inherit"` (the current workspace), `"branch"` (a new isolated
    clone, for agents that edit code in parallel), or `"share"` (a new workspace
    that shares the underlying repository). Other values are errors.
-   `schema` (required): a JSON schema (dict or string) for the agent's result.
    The agent returns the result by calling its `finish` tool, which checks it
    against the schema, and `await agent(...)` returns the parsed value. An
    agent that ends without calling `finish` fails the workflow. Use
    `{"type": "string"}` for a free-form answer.
-   `role`: an optional short title for the agent's card, such as
    `"Security reviewer"`.
-   `model`: the agent's model tier: `"inherit"` (default, your model),
    `"flash_lite"`, `"flash"`, or `"pro"`. Use a lighter tier for simple,
    high-fan-out work.
-   `fn`: usually a `lambda` that returns `agent(...)`, or an `async def`
    helper that awaits several agents. It must return something awaitable:
    an `agent()` or a call on one, a nested `parallel()` / `pipeline()`, or
    an `async def` call. Build per-item prompts and roles with f-strings.

Awaiting the same agent twice runs it once and returns the same result. An
`agent()` that is never awaited or called never runs, so always `await` it, or
pass it to `parallel` / `pipeline` and await that.

The workflow step shows one card per agent, in the order agents start, titled
with its `role`, or else the first line of its prompt, so set a role or start
each prompt with a short line that names the job.

## Agents that keep their context

When one agent should do several related turns, such as a reviewer that checks
the fixes for the bugs it found, call it instead of awaiting it. Each
`a(prompt, schema)` is lazy like an awaited `agent()` and returns that turn's
`finish` result; the agent's own `prompt`, if any, is its standing instructions
and leads the first turn. `schema` on a call defaults to the agent's. Turns on
one agent run one at a time, in the order they were started. A failed turn
raises, but the agent stays usable. An agent is either awaited or called, not
both. `del a` ends the agent, unless something else, such as a lambda, still
references it; every agent ends when the workflow ends.

```python
reviewer = agent("You review Go code for correctness.", role="Reviewer")
bugs = await reviewer("List the bugs in foo.go.", {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}})
fixes = await parallel(bugs, lambda b: agent(f"Fix: {b}", {"type": "string"}))
ok = await reviewer(f"Fixes made: {fixes}. Are all your bugs fixed?", {"type": "boolean"})
del reviewer
```

## Calling tools from the script

Where the `run_workflow` tool description lists tools for `call_tool`, the
script can call them directly:

-   `call_tool(name, **args)` returns a promise like `agent()` does. Awaiting it
    runs the tool with the arguments you would pass to it directly and returns
    the tool's output as a `str`.
-   It raises `ToolError` (with `.tool` and `.message`) if the tool fails or
    the call is denied. `.denied` is `True` when a pre-tool hook or the
    permission check rejected the call before the tool ran, so a script can
    skip denied calls and still fail on real errors.
-   The user cannot be asked anything from a workflow: a call that needs user
    approval that has not already been granted is denied.
-   Tool outputs are not shown to you unless the script logs or prints them.

## Reading earlier conversation steps

Pass inputs you already have in `Args` (or inline in the script). Use
`await trajectory(...)` when the script needs to inspect steps from earlier in
this conversation—such as mining a failed `run_command` output without
rerunning it—and pass only the relevant slice into child `agent()` prompts.

Each returned `Step` is a `dict` that also supports attribute access (missing
fields return `None` as attributes):

-   `index` (`int`): 0-based step index.
-   `type` (`str`): step type, e.g. `"USER_INPUT"`, `"PLANNER_RESPONSE"`,
    `"SYSTEM_MESSAGE"`, or `"GENERIC"` (tool calls).
-   `status` (`str`): e.g. `"DONE"`, `"ERROR"`, or `"CLEARED"`.
-   Message steps set `text` (`str`); tool steps set `tool` (`str`), `args`
    (parsed `dict`), and `output` (`str`, truncated at 200k characters).

```python
steps = await trajectory(tools=["run_command"], last=20)
errors = [s.output for s in steps if s.status == "ERROR" and s.output]
log(f"Found {len(errors)} failed command(s)")
```

`trajectory()` only returns steps before the `run_workflow` call started (steps
added while the workflow runs in the background are not included). Older tool
steps evicted from memory have `status == "CLEARED"` and `output == None`; read
the conversation's `transcript.jsonl` / `transcript_full.jsonl` when you need
cleared tool outputs or steps added after the workflow started.

## Behavior to know

-   Workflow agents are main agents, not subagents. They are hidden from the
    conversation list and reachable from the workflow step. An awaited agent
    is single-use; a called agent lasts until deleted or the workflow ends.
-   `await agent(...)` returns when the agent's run ends, with the result it
    passed to `finish`.
-   If one agent in `parallel` fails, the whole call fails and the other agents
    in it are cancelled. Stopping the parent conversation stops all running
    workflow agents.
-   Agents do not see the script or each other. Put all the context an agent
    needs in its prompt, and ask for a short, well-defined output.

## Example

Fan out over a list that an agent produces:

```python
phase("Discover")
files = await agent(
    "List the Go files under pkg/foo that call Bar(). Paths only.",
    schema={"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
)

phase("Review")
reviews = await parallel(files, lambda f: agent(
    f"Review {f} for misuse of Bar(). Reply in 3 bullets or 'OK'.",
    schema={"type": "string"},
    role=f"Review {f}",
))
for r in reviews:
    log(r)
```

# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 ObiWindu <Obi.wandu@proton.me>
# SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-2.1-or-later
#
# Bundle the latest Kate (built via Craft) with this plugin on Windows.
#
# Result: packaging\dist\kate-bundle-<ver>-windows-<arch>.zip containing:
#   kateai.dll        # this plugin (MSVC ABI, matches Craft Kate)
#   install.ps1       # installs kateai.dll next to Kate (see packaging\windows)
#   README.txt        # pairs with the latest Kate installer built by Craft
# plus, when produced: the Craft Kate installer (kate-*.exe) from C:\CraftRoot\tmp
#
# Usage: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File packaging\bundle-kate-windows.ps1 `
#            [-Out <file>] [-SkipKate]
[CmdletBinding()]
param(
    [string] $Out = "",
    [switch] $SkipKate,
    [string] $CraftRoot = "C:\CraftRoot"
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$Root = (Resolve-Path (Join-Path $PSScriptRoot "..")).Path
Set-Location $Root

# Craft's MSVC toolchain aborts when sh.exe or a foreign gcc sits in PATH,
# and the same pollution breaks its Visual Studio detection. The hosted
# runner ships Git's sh (Git\bin and Git\usr\bin, depending on image),
# MinGW and Strawberry Perl gcc. Strip those entries (keeping Git\cmd for
# git.exe); Craft brings its own toolchain and the runner's cmake/ninja
# stay on PATH.
$env:PATH = ($env:PATH -split ';' | Where-Object {
    $_ -and $_ -notmatch '(?i)Git\\(bin|usr\\bin)' -and $_ -notmatch '(?i)mingw|strawberry'
}) -join ';'

$m = Select-String -Path (Join-Path $Root "CMakeLists.txt") -Pattern 'project\(kateai VERSION ([^ ]+)' | Select-Object -First 1
$version = "0.1.0"
if ($m) { $version = $m.Matches[0].Groups[1].Value }
$arch = $env:PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE
if (-not $arch) { $arch = "amd64" }
if (-not $Out) {
    $Out = Join-Path $Root "packaging\dist\kate-bundle-$version-windows-$arch.zip"
}

$craftEnv = Join-Path $CraftRoot "craft\craftenv.ps1"
if (-not (Test-Path $craftEnv)) {
    # Each CI job runs on a fresh VM, so the Craft stack built by
    # windows-build.ps1 is not here: bootstrap it on demand.
    Write-Host "==> Bootstrapping KDE Craft (accepting defaults)"
    # The hosted runner already enforces Bypass via a higher-precedence
    # scope, which makes this assignment throw: not fatal, Bypass is
    # exactly what we need to run the installer below.
    try {
        Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope CurrentUser RemoteSigned -Force
    } catch {
        Write-Host "Execution policy is host-managed; continuing with the effective Bypass policy."
    }
    python.exe -m pip install --upgrade certifi
    # -root skips the install-path prompt; -use-defaults is forwarded to
    # CraftBootstrap.py (arch/compiler auto-detected). Downloaded first so
    # the exact command line shows in the log instead of hiding in iex.
    $installer = Join-Path ([IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) "install_craft.ps1"
    (New-Object net.webclient).DownloadFile(
        'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KDE/craft/master/setup/install_craft.ps1', $installer)
    if ($env:CI -eq 'true' -and (Test-Path $CraftRoot)) {
        # The installer loops forever on a non-empty target dir when there
        # is no console to answer its prompt; CI VMs are disposable.
        Write-Host "Removing pre-existing $CraftRoot for a clean Craft bootstrap."
        Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $CraftRoot
    }
    & $installer -root $CraftRoot -use-defaults
}
if (-not (Test-Path $craftEnv)) {
    throw "KDE Craft not found at $CraftRoot. Install it first, see https://develop.kde.org/docs/getting-started/building/craft/"
}
# Craft's craftenv.ps1 sanitizes the environment by removing a fixed list of
# variables (including GITHUB_ACTION_REF). On some GitHub runners that
# variable is not defined, which makes Remove-Item throw and abort the build.
foreach ($name in @("GITHUB_ACTION_REF", "GITHUB_ACTION", "GITHUB_ACTION_PATH", "GITHUB_ACTION_REPOSITORY", "GITHUB_BASE_REF", "GITHUB_HEAD_REF", "GITHUB_REF", "GITHUB_SHA")) {
    if (-not (Test-Path "Env:$name")) {
        Set-Item "Env:$name" ""
    }
}
if (Test-Path $craftEnv) {
    $content = Get-Content $craftEnv -Raw
    $content = $content.Replace('Remove-Item ("ENV:{0}" -f ${_}.Name)', 'Remove-Item ("ENV:{0}" -f ${_}.Name) -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue')
    $content = $content.Replace('$python = (Get-Command "$env:KDEROOT/dev-utils/bin/python3" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue).Source', '$python = $env:CRAFT_PYTHON')
    Set-Content $craftEnv $content
}
# Dot-source: the env script must mutate THIS session (PATH, KDEROOT, craft/cs
# functions). `&` would run it in a child scope and lose them.
$prevEap = $ErrorActionPreference
$ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"
try {
    . $craftEnv
} finally {
    $ErrorActionPreference = $prevEap
}

# gettext's AM_ICONV runs a runtime probe that often fails to execute on the
# Windows/Craft host, making HAVE_ICONV=0 and breaking the libtextstyle link
# (LNK2001: iconv_ostream_create). Preset the cache variables and build
# iconv first, as in packaging\ci\windows-build.ps1.
$env:am_cv_func_iconv = "yes"
$env:am_cv_func_iconv_works = "yes"
$env:am_cv_lib_iconv = "yes"

# Make the func/lib cache variables explicit in Craft's gettext blueprint too
# (it only presets works), so a failed link probe cannot reset HAVE_ICONV.
$gettextBlueprint = Get-ChildItem -Path $CraftRoot -Recurse -Filter gettext.py -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1
if ($gettextBlueprint) {
    $bp = Get-Content $gettextBlueprint.FullName -Raw
    if ($bp -notmatch 'am_cv_func_iconv=yes') {
        $bp = $bp -replace '"am_cv_func_iconv_works=yes"', '"am_cv_func_iconv=yes", "am_cv_func_iconv_works=yes", "am_cv_lib_iconv=yes"'
        Set-Content -Path $gettextBlueprint.FullName -Value $bp
    }
}
Get-ChildItem -Path $CraftRoot -Recurse -Filter config.cache -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue |
    Where-Object { $_.FullName -match 'gettext' } |
    Remove-Item -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue

craft libs/iconv
if (-not $?) { throw "craft libs/iconv failed" }

if (-not $SkipKate) {
    Write-Host "==> Building latest Kate via Craft"
    craft kate
    if (-not $?) { throw "craft kate failed" }
}

# Build the plugin against the Craft prefix (same flow as windows-build.ps1).
Write-Host "==> Building plugin against $CraftRoot"
& (Join-Path $Root "packaging\ci\windows-build.ps1") -BuildType Release -ArtifactsDir (Join-Path $Root "artifacts-windows-tmp")

$stage = Join-Path ([System.IO.Path]::GetTempPath()) ([System.IO.Path]::GetRandomFileName())
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $stage | Out-Null
Copy-Item -Force (Join-Path $Root "artifacts-windows-tmp\kateai.dll") (Join-Path $stage "kateai.dll")
Copy-Item -Force (Join-Path $Root "packaging\windows\install.ps1") (Join-Path $stage "install.ps1")
@"
Kate AI plugin for Kate on Windows (v$version).

Pairs with the latest Kate. Either:
  1. Install Kate via Craft (craft kate), or download it from
     https://download.kde.org/stable/kate/ — then run:
       powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1
  2. Or copy kateai.dll next to Kate's kf6\ktexteditor plugin directory.
"@ | Out-File -Encoding utf8 (Join-Path $stage "README.txt")

# Also pick up a Craft-built Kate installer when present: that plus this zip
# is the full "latest Kate bundled with the plugin" set for the release.
$kateInstallers = @()
$tmpDir = Join-Path $CraftRoot "tmp"
if (Test-Path $tmpDir) {
    $kateInstallers = @(Get-ChildItem -Path $tmpDir -Filter "kate-*.exe" | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 1)
    if (-not $kateInstallers -or $kateInstallers.Count -eq 0) {
        Write-Host "No Craft Kate installer in $tmpDir; building one with: craft --package kate"
        craft --package kate
        $kateInstallers = @(Get-ChildItem -Path $tmpDir -Filter "kate-*.exe" | Sort-Object LastWriteTime -Descending | Select-Object -First 1)
    }
}

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path (Split-Path $Out) | Out-Null
if (Test-Path $Out) { Remove-Item -Force $Out }
Compress-Archive -Path (Join-Path $stage "*") -DestinationPath $Out
Get-Item $Out
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $stage
Remove-Item -Recurse -Force (Join-Path $Root "artifacts-windows-tmp")
foreach ($installer in $kateInstallers) {
    if ($installer) {
        Copy-Item -Force $installer.FullName (Join-Path (Split-Path $Out) $installer.Name)
        Get-Item (Join-Path (Split-Path $Out) $installer.Name)
    }
}
Write-Host "Bundle ready: $Out"

#pragma once

#include "types.h"

#include <QList>
#include <QString>

namespace KateAi
{

/**
 * How a transcript is anchored within its viewport when the conversation is
 * shorter than the panel.
 *
 * Top is a document: the first message is flush against the top and the slack
 * falls away below, so the thread reads oldest-to-newest downward. Bottom is a
 * composer-pinned chat: the newest message sits against the input and the slack
 * collects above.
 *
 * The insert index for a new message has to land on the growing side of the
 * stretch: before it under Top, after it under Bottom. Getting that backwards
 * puts every new message on the far side of the slack, so user turns pile up
 * at the bottom of the viewport instead of in chronological order.
 *
 * Naming the two states keeps the choice explicit at the call sites that depend
 * on it.
 */
enum class TranscriptAnchor {
    Bottom,
    Top,
};

/**
 * Where in the transcript layout a newly appended message must be inserted.
 *
 * `spacerIndex` is the layout index of the stretch item (-1 when there is none)
 * and `indicatorsIndex` the index of the pinned thinking/working row (-1 when it
 * is absent). The result is always in [0, count].
 *
 * The rule: land on the far side of the stretch from the anchor, and always
 * before the indicator row, which stays last so live status sits under the
 * newest turn.
 */
int transcriptInsertIndexFor(TranscriptAnchor anchor, int spacerIndex, int indicatorsIndex, int count);

/**
 * Whether the transcript should follow new content, given where the scrollbar
 * currently sits.
 *
 * A short tail (within `FollowThresholdPx` of the end) counts as following; past
 * that the user has scrolled away and the panel should stop yanking the viewport
 * and offer "jump to latest" instead.
 */
bool transcriptShouldFollowTail(int scrollbarValue, int scrollbarMaximum);

} // namespace KateAi

# Shared platform helpers for install.sh / uninstall.sh / build.sh.
# Not meant to be run directly.

kateai_uname() {
    uname -s 2>/dev/null || echo unknown
}

kateai_jobs() {
    if command -v nproc >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        nproc
    elif command -v sysctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        sysctl -n hw.ncpu 2>/dev/null || echo 4
    else
        echo 4
    fi
}

kateai_plugin_name() {
    case "$(kateai_uname)" in
        MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*|Windows_NT) echo kateai.dll ;;
        *) echo kateai.so ;;
    esac
}

kateai_user_plugin_dir() {
    case "$(kateai_uname)" in
        Darwin)
            echo "${HOME}/Library/Application Support/kate/lib/qt6/plugins"
            ;;
        MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*|Windows_NT)
            echo "${LOCALAPPDATA:-${HOME}/AppData/Local}/KateAI/plugins"
            ;;
        *)
            echo "${HOME}/.local/lib/qt6/plugins"
            ;;
    esac
}

kateai_os_release_id() {
    if [[ -r /etc/os-release ]]; then
        # shellcheck disable=SC1091
        . /etc/os-release
        echo "${ID:-}"
    fi
}

kateai_os_release_like() {
    if [[ -r /etc/os-release ]]; then
        # shellcheck disable=SC1091
        . /etc/os-release
        echo "${ID_LIKE:-} ${ID:-} ${VARIANT_ID:-} ${VARIANT:-}"
    fi
}

kateai_family() {
    case "$(kateai_uname)" in
        Darwin) echo macos; return ;;
        MINGW*|MSYS*|CYGWIN*|Windows_NT) echo windows; return ;;
    esac
    local like
    like="$(kateai_os_release_like | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]')"
    case " ${like} " in
        *" arch "*|*" cachyos "*|*" manjaro "*|*" endeavouros "*) echo arch ;;
        *" fedora "*|*" asahi "*|*" rhel "*|*" centos "*) echo fedora ;;
        *" debian "*|*" ubuntu "*) echo debian ;;
        *) echo linux ;;
    esac
}

kateai_ubuntu_ok() {
    if [[ ! -r /etc/os-release ]]; then
        return 1
    fi
    # shellcheck disable=SC1091
    . /etc/os-release
    if [[ "${ID:-}" == "debian" ]]; then
        return 0
    fi
    if [[ "${ID:-}" != "ubuntu" && "${ID_LIKE:-}" != *ubuntu* ]]; then
        return 1
    fi
    local ver="${VERSION_ID:-0}"
    local major minor
    major="${ver%%.*}"
    minor="${ver#*.}"
    minor="${minor%%.*}"
    if [[ "${major}" -gt 25 ]]; then
        return 0
    fi
    if [[ "${major}" -eq 25 && "${minor:-0}" -ge 4 ]]; then
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

# Arch / CachyOS / Manjaro package names.
kateai_arch_packages() {
    printf '%s\n' \
        kate extra-cmake-modules cmake ninja gcc \
        qt6-base ktexteditor kcoreaddons ki18n \
        kxmlgui kconfigwidgets kconfig kwidgetsaddons \
        bubblewrap
}

kateai_fedora_packages() {
    printf '%s\n' \
        kate extra-cmake-modules cmake gcc-c++ ninja-build \
        qt6-qtbase-devel kf6-ktexteditor-devel kf6-kcoreaddons-devel \
        kf6-ki18n-devel kf6-kxmlgui-devel kf6-kconfigwidgets-devel \
        kf6-kconfig-devel kf6-kwidgetsaddons-devel \
        bubblewrap
}

kateai_debian_packages() {
    printf '%s\n' \
        kate cmake extra-cmake-modules ninja-build g++ pkg-config \
        qt6-base-dev qt6-base-dev-tools qt6-tools-dev \
        libkf6texteditor-dev libkf6coreaddons-dev libkf6i18n-dev \
        libkf6xmlgui-dev libkf6configwidgets-dev libkf6config-dev \
        libkf6widgetsaddons-dev \
        bubblewrap
}

kateai_macos_brew_packages() {
    printf '%s\n' \
        cmake extra-cmake-modules ninja qtbase \
        kcoreaddons ki18n kconfig kconfigwidgets kxmlgui kwidgetsaddons
}

kateai_priv() {
    if [[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]]; then
        "$@"
    elif command -v sudo >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        sudo "$@"
    else
        echo "Need root to run: $*" >&2
        return 1
    fi
}

kateai_install_deps() {
    local family
    family="$(kateai_family)"
    case "${family}" in
        arch)
            kateai_priv pacman -S --needed --noconfirm $(kateai_arch_packages)
            ;;
        fedora)
            if command -v dnf5 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                kateai_priv dnf5 install -y $(kateai_fedora_packages)
            elif command -v dnf >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                kateai_priv dnf install -y $(kateai_fedora_packages)
            else
                echo "dnf is required on Fedora / Asahi." >&2
                return 1
            fi
            ;;
        debian)
            if ! kateai_ubuntu_ok; then
                echo "Debian/Ubuntu packages target Ubuntu 25.04+ (KF6). This release may be too old." >&2
            fi
            kateai_priv apt-get update
            kateai_priv apt-get install -y $(kateai_debian_packages)
            ;;
        macos)
            if ! command -v brew >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "Homebrew is required on macOS. Install it from https://brew.sh" >&2
                return 1
            fi
            brew install $(kateai_macos_brew_packages)
            if ! brew list --cask kate >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                brew install --cask kate
            fi
            echo
            echo "ktexteditor headers are not in Homebrew. Building against Homebrew KF6"
            echo "may not load in the Kate.app cask. Prefer KDE Craft for a matching ABI:"
            echo "  https://develop.kde.org/docs/getting-started/building/craft/"
            echo "The installer will still copy a built plugin into Kate.app when possible."
            ;;
        windows)
            echo "On Windows, build with KDE Craft so the plugin matches Kate's ABI." >&2
            echo "See packaging/windows/install.ps1" >&2
            return 1
            ;;
        *)
            echo "No packaged dependencies for this OS. Install Kate, Qt 6.5+, KF6, CMake 3.25+, and bubblewrap (Linux)." >&2
            return 1
            ;;
    esac
}

kateai_find_built_plugin() {
    local build_dir="$1"
    local name
    name="$(kateai_plugin_name)"
    if [[ -f "${build_dir}/bin/kf6/ktexteditor/${name}" ]]; then
        printf '%s\n' "${build_dir}/bin/kf6/ktexteditor/${name}"
        return 0
    fi
    local found
    found="$(find "${build_dir}" \( -name kateai.so -o -name kateai.dll -o -name kateai.dylib \) -print -quit 2>/dev/null || true)"
    if [[ -n "${found}" && -f "${found}" ]]; then
        printf '%s\n' "${found}"
        return 0
    fi
    return 1
}

kateai_macos_kate_plugin_dirs() {
    local app dir
    for app in \
        "/Applications/Kate.app" \
        "/Applications/kate.app" \
        "${HOME}/Applications/Kate.app" \
        "${HOME}/Applications/kate.app"; do
        if [[ -d "${app}" ]]; then
            while IFS= read -r dir; do
                printf '%s\n' "${dir}"
            done < <(find "${app}/Contents" -type d -name ktexteditor 2>/dev/null || true)
            printf '%s\n' "${app}/Contents/PlugIns/kf6/ktexteditor"
            printf '%s\n' "${app}/Contents/lib/plugins/kf6/ktexteditor"
        fi
    done
}

kateai_write_macos_launch_agent() {
    local plugin_dir="$1"
    local dest="${HOME}/Library/LaunchAgents/org.kateai.qtpluginpath.plist"
    mkdir -p "${HOME}/Library/LaunchAgents"
    cat > "${dest}" <<EOF
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0">
<dict>
    <key>Label</key>
    <string>org.kateai.qtpluginpath</string>
    <key>ProgramArguments</key>
    <array>
        <string>/bin/launchctl</string>
        <string>setenv</string>
        <string>QT_PLUGIN_PATH</string>
        <string>${plugin_dir}</string>
    </array>
    <key>RunAtLoad</key>
    <true/>
</dict>
</plist>
EOF
    chmod 600 "${dest}"
    launchctl unload "${dest}" 2>/dev/null || true
    launchctl load "${dest}" 2>/dev/null || true
    launchctl setenv QT_PLUGIN_PATH "${plugin_dir}" 2>/dev/null || true
    echo "${dest}"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build a distro package from this tree (Arch pkg.tar.zst, Fedora rpm, Debian deb).
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "${ROOT}"
# shellcheck source=scripts/kateai-platform.sh
source "${ROOT}/scripts/kateai-platform.sh"

FAMILY="${1:-$(kateai_family)}"
TARBALL="$("${ROOT}/packaging/mk-source-tarball.sh")"
VERSION="$(basename "${TARBALL}" .tar.gz)"
VERSION="${VERSION#kateai-}"
WORKDIR="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "${WORKDIR}"' EXIT

case "${FAMILY}" in
    arch)
        cp -a "${ROOT}/packaging/arch/." "${WORKDIR}/"
        cp -f "${TARBALL}" "${WORKDIR}/kateai-${VERSION}.tar.gz"
        # makepkg 7+ sandboxes the build with Landlock/bubblewrap, which
        # fails inside unprivileged Docker containers. Use --nosandbox
        # when the flag is available (pacman 7.0+, 2025).
        makepkg_extra=""
        if makepkg --help 2>&1 | grep -q -- '--nosandbox'; then
            makepkg_extra="--nosandbox"
        fi
        if [[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]]; then
            # makepkg refuses to run as root (CI containers are root): build
            # as an unprivileged user instead. Deps are already installed
            # system-wide, so no -s (sudo pacman) round-trip is needed.
            id builder >/dev/null 2>&1 || useradd -m builder
            chown -R builder:builder "${WORKDIR}"
            su builder -s /bin/bash -c "cd '${WORKDIR}' && makepkg -f --noconfirm ${makepkg_extra}"
        else
            (cd "${WORKDIR}" && makepkg -f --noconfirm ${makepkg_extra})
        fi
        mkdir -p "${ROOT}/packaging/dist"
        cp -f "${WORKDIR}"/*.pkg.tar.* "${ROOT}/packaging/dist/"
        echo "Arch package(s) in ${ROOT}/packaging/dist/"
        ls -l "${ROOT}/packaging/dist"/*.pkg.tar.*
        ;;
    fedora)
        mkdir -p "${WORKDIR}/SOURCES" "${WORKDIR}/SPECS" "${WORKDIR}/BUILD" "${WORKDIR}/RPMS" "${WORKDIR}/SRPMS"
        cp -f "${TARBALL}" "${WORKDIR}/SOURCES/"
        cp -f "${ROOT}/packaging/fedora/kateai.spec" "${WORKDIR}/SPECS/"
        rpmbuild \
            --define "_topdir ${WORKDIR}" \
            -ba "${WORKDIR}/SPECS/kateai.spec"
        mkdir -p "${ROOT}/packaging/dist"
        find "${WORKDIR}/RPMS" "${WORKDIR}/SRPMS" -type f -name '*.rpm' -exec cp -f {} "${ROOT}/packaging/dist/" \;
        echo "RPM package(s) in ${ROOT}/packaging/dist/"
        ls -l "${ROOT}/packaging/dist"/*.rpm
        ;;
    debian)
        tar -C "${WORKDIR}" -xzf "${TARBALL}"
        SRC="${WORKDIR}/kateai-${VERSION}"
        (cd "${SRC}" && dpkg-buildpackage -us -uc -b)
        mkdir -p "${ROOT}/packaging/dist"
        cp -f "${WORKDIR}"/*.deb "${ROOT}/packaging/dist/" 2>/dev/null || true
        echo "Debian package(s) in ${ROOT}/packaging/dist/"
        ls -l "${ROOT}/packaging/dist"/*.deb
        ;;
    macos)
        # Plugin zip for macOS: Homebrew Kate + KF6 build (see packaging/ci/macos-build.sh).
        VERSION="$(sed -n 's/^project(kateai VERSION \([^ ]*\).*/\1/p' "${ROOT}/CMakeLists.txt" | head -1)"
        VERSION="${VERSION:-0.1.0}"
        "${ROOT}/packaging/ci/macos-build.sh" --build-type Release --artifacts-dir "${ROOT}/artifacts-macos-tmp"
        mkdir -p "${ROOT}/packaging/dist"
        OUT="${ROOT}/packaging/dist/kateai-${VERSION}-macos-$(uname -m).zip"
        rm -f "${OUT}"
        (cd "${ROOT}/artifacts-macos-tmp" && zip -j "${OUT}" kateai.so)
        rm -rf "${ROOT}/artifacts-macos-tmp"
        echo "macOS package: ${OUT}"
        ls -l "${OUT}"
        ;;
    windows)
        echo "On Windows, build with KDE Craft (matching MSVC ABI):" >&2
        echo "  powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File packaging\\ci\\windows-build.ps1" >&2
        echo "Bundle latest Kate + plugin with:" >&2
        echo "  powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File packaging\\bundle-kate-windows.ps1" >&2
        exit 1
        ;;
    *)
        echo "No package recipe for family '${FAMILY}'." >&2
        echo "Supported: arch (CachyOS, Manjaro), fedora (Asahi), debian (Ubuntu 25.04+)." >&2
        exit 1
        ;;
esac
