nodes.content:
# Kate AI — Architecture

Developer map of the plugin. User-facing documentation lives in `README.md`.

## Layout

```
src/
  plugin.cpp / pluginview.cpp     KTextEditor plugin + tool view, actions, shortcuts
  kateaicommand.cpp               the ":kateai" editor command-line command
  chatwidget.cpp                  transcript, composer, model picker, mode menus
  toolcallwidget.cpp              one tool-call card (header, diff, output, copy)
  turnstatus.cpp                  live status strip (elapsed time, current activity)
  agentloop.cpp                   the turn: prompt -> model -> tools -> model -> ...
  llmclient.cpp / acpclient.cpp   provider transports (HTTP formats, native ACP)
  tools.cpp / sandbox.cpp         every built-in tool and the path sandbox around them
  modes.cpp                       built-in + .kateai/modes/ mode definitions
  sessionstore.cpp                conversation persistence (SQLite)
  contextmanager.cpp              prompt assembly, context window, compaction
  graph/projectgraph.cpp          workspace structure graph
  mcp.cpp                         Model Context Protocol stdio clients
  lsp.h / lsp.cpp                 the editor's language-server surface (LspProvider) the core queries
  katelspbridge.cpp               Kate-facing LspProvider: probes the katelspclientplugin at runtime,
                                  reads Error/Warning document marks, captures LSP messages
  checkpoint.cpp                  pre-turn shadow-git snapshots
  edittracker.cpp                 review queue for agent edits
  completionengine.cpp / editranges.cpp  in-editor completions (core half): FIM/chat prompts, budgets, MovingCursor-anchored edit ranges
  editorassist.cpp               in-editor pixels: ghost text, Tab accept, hover hints, one per main window
tests/                            one QTest binary per component (see below)
```

Two link targets:

- **`kateai_core`** (static lib) — everything without a Kate GUI dependency.
  AgentLoop, LlmClient, AcpClient, ToolRunner, Sandbox, SessionStore, ProjectGraph,
  ModeRegistry. Tests link against this.
- **`kateai`** (KTextEditor plugin) — Kate-facing widgets only: ChatWidget,
  ToolCallWidget, TurnStatus, ConfigPage, PluginView.

Rule of thumb: new logic that a test can drive belongs in `kateai_core`; new
pixels belong in `kateai`.

## The turn

`AgentLoop` owns one conversation. The lifecycle:

1. `submit()` appends the user message and builds the system prompt
   (`buildSystemPrompt()`): mode persona, rules (`.kateai/`, `KATEAI.md`), editor
   context, project graph summary, sandbox/permission summary.
2. `LlmClient::complete()` streams tokens. Thinking deltas and content deltas
   arrive separately, so the UI can render hidden reasoning collapsibly.
3. Tool calls are executed through `ToolRunner`, gated by `PermissionPolicy`
   (Ask / AcceptEdits / AlwaysApprove) and `Sandbox` (path + command checks).
   File-mutating calls are snapshotted by `CheckpointManager` first and queued
   into `EditTracker` under AcceptEdits.
4. Tool results go back to the model; the loop repeats until the model finishes
   or a budget (`maxModelRequests`, `maxToolCalls`) is exhausted.

Everything is asynchronous: one `bash` process runs detached, MCP calls run over
stdio JSON-RPC, sub-agents (`new_task`) run as nested `AgentLoop`s.

## ACP tool integration

When the provider is an ACP agent (`usesAcpNative`), `AgentLoop` delegates the
turn to `AcpClient` instead of `LlmClient`. Tool calls arrive as
`session/update` notifications (`tool_call`, `tool_call_update`); Kate renders
cards and tracks edits from those.

### Name normalisation

ACP agents use their own tool names (`fs/read_text_file`, `terminal/exec`,
`edit`, `write`, `apply_patch`, …). `canonicalToolName()` in `types.cpp` maps
these to KateAI's canonical names (`read_file`, `bash`, `edit_file`, `write_file`,
…) on ingest in `AcpClient::permissionFromToolCall()`. MCP-prefixed names
(`mcp__*`) are preserved. The canonical name drives `ToolAccess`, `ChatTheme`,
`shellCommandFor`, edit tracking, and history restoration; the original name is
kept in `PermissionRequest::originalToolName` for display/debugging.

A call that names no tool falls back to its ACP `kind` (`read` → `read_file`,
`search` → `grep`, `fetch` → `web_fetch`), and a built-in name in another case
(`Grep`, `BASH`) is the same tool.

### Parsing & diffs

`permissionFromToolCall()` normalises `rawInput` (object/string/array), scans
`content[]` and `locations[]` for paths and diff blocks, resolves relative paths
against the workspace, and builds a unified diff from `oldText`/`newText` or
`old_string`/`new_string` (camelCase and snake_case both accepted). Each diff is
kept with the file it edits: the primary diff is the one for the primary file,
and the others go to `additionalPaths`/`additionalDiffs` in matching order. A
diff that arrived only as a content block is also written into the stored
arguments, so a restored transcript rebuilds the same card.

`tool_call_update` merges what an update adds into the live entry
(`mergeToolCallDetails`) and emits `toolDetailsChanged` when a diff or path
arrives late, so the card and the review entry catch up. Progress is aggregated
(cumulative or delta).

### Permissions

`AcpClient::handleRequestPermission()` merges the request with the tool call
the agent already announced (a request often names only the call's id) and
emits `permissionNeeded`. `AgentLoop::acpAutoDecision()` is the one decision
point for ACP, the same policy native turns use: session grants, the
auto-approve list, AlwaysApprove and AcceptEdits allow, and everything else
asks the user. A tool the mode does not allow is not declined here; the
permission card still lets you approve it.

`acpToolPermitted()` (in `modes.cpp`) judges a tool the mode allows: a tool Kate
knows is judged by its name, and an agent's own tool by what it does (running a
command needs the command tool, changing a file needs the edit tools, anything
else is not restricted). Reasoning is always allowed.

The agent runs its own tools, so Kate cannot stop a tool that asks no permission;
it shows a notice instead, and the permission card still lets you approve a tool
the active mode does not list.

### Terminals

A terminal the agent creates with `terminal/create` and embeds in a tool call
(`{type: "terminal", terminalId}`) is linked to that call. Its output streams
into the card while the command runs, and the final result falls back to that
output. The terminal reference itself is never printed as output.

### Edit tracking

In every permission mode for ACP turns, `ChatWidget` tracks mutations detected
by protocol kind, `mutatesFiles`, diff presence, or name heuristics. Multi-file
edits are tracked per file. Snapshots are taken at `toolStarted`; paths are
resolved against the workspace.

### History restoration

`ChatWidget::restoreHistoricalTool()` canonicalises the tool name and reconstructs
diffs from stored arguments for native and ACP shapes, sets the file path for
language highlighting, and restores subtask/suggestion cards.

### Client methods

Kate exposes `fs/read_text_file`, `fs/write_text_file`, `terminal/*`, and its own
`_kateai/query_project_graph`, `_kateai/write_plan_file`, `_kateai/suggest`,
`_kateai/ask_user`, `_kateai/todo_write`, `_kateai/todo_read`, and the `lsp_*`
family (`_kateai/lsp_diagnostics`, `_kateai/lsp_symbols`, `_kateai/lsp_hover`,
`_kateai/lsp_definition`, `_kateai/lsp_references`, `_kateai/lsp_code_actions`).
The extension names are the ones the protocol reserves for
extensions; they are advertised in the `initialize` capabilities under `_meta`
(`com.kateai/methods`). The bare names (`write_plan_file`, …) still reach the
same handlers. Results are formatted to match native tool output, including the
pagination note on reads. `suggest` emits `suggestionPosted` which `ChatWidget`
turns into a suggestion card; `ask_user` parks the RPC, emits `questionAsked`
(the same signal the native `question` tool drives), and answers the RPC from
`AgentLoop::answerQuestion` — the v2-draft `elicitation/create` reaches the same
path.

Agents that expose their own question/suggestion tools are normalized too:
`permissionFromToolCall()` accepts the flat `{question, options}` shape, the
Claude/OpenCode `{questions:[{question, options:[{label}]}]}` shape and plain
text, and canonicalizes names like `suggestion`, `ask_question`,
`ask_user_question` or a title that says "ask user". A question tool call shows
the same dock card; because ACP has no client-to-agent tool-result channel, its
answer is sent as the next user prompt after the current turn closes. A
`session/request_permission` whose options are answer labels rather than
allow/reject kinds is shown as a question card too, and the selected chip is
returned as the permission request's `optionId`. A suggestion tool call becomes
a normal suggestion card through `toolStarted`. `todo_write`/`todo_read` share the native todo store through a
getter/setter pair installed by `AgentLoop::syncAcpClient`, and emit
`todosChanged`, which the loop forwards as `planUpdated` so `TodoWidget` renders
them. Slash commands are stored and announced via `availableCommandsChanged`:
the `session/new`/`session/resume` `availableCommands` field is read, and the
protocol's `session/update` → `available_commands_update` variant replaces the
list (the old top-level notification is accepted as a compatibility fallback).

### Protocol negotiation and agent quirks

`initialize` sends Kate's maximum `protocolVersion` and accepts the agent's
answer clamped to what Kate speaks (a v2 agent is clamped to v1 and simply does
not get the v2 features; elicitation is enabled when the agent advertises the
`elicitation` capability). Per-agent launch quirks (an `acp` subcommand,
npm-token stripping, `--model` support, sanitizer flags, Zed clientInfo spoof)
live in `acpAgentQuirks()` keyed by registry id, so agents installed from the
ACP registry get the same treatment as the built-in presets. Registry `env`
arrays are merged into the agent process environment in `processEnvironment()`.
Package-distribution agents are launched via `npx --yes <pkg>@<version>` /
`uvx <pkg>@<version>` with no global install.

## LSP bridge

`LspProvider` (lsp.h) is the interface the core (`ToolRunner`, `AcpClient`)
queries for language-server data: availability, per-file diagnostics, server
messages, and optional symbols/hover/definition/references/code-action answers.
`KateLspBridge` (katelspbridge.cpp) implements it against Kate's LSP client
plugin: it looks up `katelspclientplugin` through the application plugin list
(the same string-based, runtime-probed pattern used for `kateprojectplugin`),
captures its public `showMessage` signal, and derives diagnostics from the
Error/Warning marks of open documents, re-scanned on `marksChanged` plus a
slow poll so `diagnosticsChanged` fires. When the plugin is absent or changes
its internals, `isAvailable()` is false and the `lsp_*` tools report the
feature as unavailable instead of failing; symbol/hover/definition/references
then fall back to the project graph (which now indexes per-file symbols with
line ranges) and plain text search. The `lsp_*` tools are read-only, so they
are allowed in plan/ask/architect/orchestrator modes and never prompt.

Agents do not receive Kate's system prompt, so the first prompt of each ACP
session starts with a notes block: the user's global rules and extra system
prompt (except for Grok, which gets them through `_meta`), and the list of
Kate's client methods. The notes are sent once per session.

## Settings and modes

`Settings` is one flat struct persisted by `settings.cpp` (KConfig). Modes
(`modes.cpp`) narrow **which tools** the model may call via `ToolAccess`
(exact names + prefixes for MCP tools) and may override the **sampling knobs**:

```
mode.temperature / mode.topP   # -1 = not set, use the global Settings value
```

`ModeRegistry::settingsForMode()` merges the two; `AgentLoop` hands the merged
copy to `LlmClient` and keeps the raw struct for the config page, so an override
never leaks back into saved settings. Built-in modes set neither override.

## Sandbox invariants

`Sandbox::normalizePath()` is the single gate for file tools:

- Relative paths resolve against the workspace root.
- Symlinks are resolved with `canonicalFilePath()`, and containment is
  re-checked **after** resolution — the classic escape (`workspace/link ->
  /etc`) is refused for writes in every profile but `Off`.
- Deny globs (`.env`, `**/.ssh/**`) apply on top of the profile.
- Commands are classified read-only / dangerous / always-denied, and wrapped in
  bubblewrap under Workspace/Strict profiles.

When touching this code, add cases to `tests/test_sandbox.cpp` — the escape
tests there are the regression net for TOCTOU-style changes.

## Tool contract

`tools.cpp` implements the tool set advertised by `toolDefinitions()` in
`types.cpp` (name, description, JSON schema, access group): file tools,
`apply_patch` (multi-file unified diff, atomic — parsed by `parseUnifiedPatch`/
`applyPatchToContent` in `types.cpp`, shared with the ACP ingest path),
`bash`, web tools, the `lsp_*` family, `query_project_graph`, and the UI-state
tools `write_plan_file`, `suggest`, `question`, `todo_write`/`todo_read`,
`think`, `exit_plan_mode`, plus `new_task` and `goal_report`. Conventions:

- Tools return a `ToolResult` with `output` (formatted, clipped) and `rawOutput`.
- `clip()` truncates at 80 KB **keeping head and tail** — for a command whose
  error summary is its last line, a head-only clip would throw away the answer.
- `read_file` paginates; long results end with a `more line(s) not shown` note
  that tells the model the next `offset`.
- `multi_edit_file` applies a batch atomically and **rejects overlapping edits**:
  each edit must target text none of the earlier ones consumed or produced,
  because matches are found in the working string after those edits.
- `apply_patch` plans every file before writing, accepts the standard
  `@@ -0,0` new-file range, distinguishes an empty file from a deletion, and
  rolls back already-written files if a later write fails.
- Read-only disk tools (`list_dir`, `grep`, `glob`) are offloaded to a worker
  thread by `ToolRunner::runReadToolAsync` through a bridge that never touches
  KTextEditor documents, emitting `bashProgress`/`bashFinished`, so a long
  search streams instead of freezing the transcript. `read_file` stays
  synchronous because it must see the editor's unsaved buffer; tools that touch
  the project graph or the LSP provider stay synchronous too. A stop cancels
  the in-flight jobs and a turn generation marks late results stale.

## UI structure

- `ChatWidget` builds the transcript as a vertical list of widgets (user
  bubbles, assistant text, thinking blocks, plan checklists, tool cards,
  suggestion/question cards, sub-task cards) inside a `QScrollArea`.
- Tool cards (`ToolCallWidget`) are stateful: header summary, expand/collapse,
  diff preview, live output while running, copy button (full output, not the
  truncated view), and a file-path jump signal wired to `openFileAtLineRequested`
  so a click opens the file in Kate at that line.
- The **intent dock** above the composer holds anything awaiting the user
  (approval rows, question cards, live sub-agent cards); retired widgets move
  back into the transcript in place. A running sub-agent card streams its tool
  starts/finishes, streamed command output, progress text and latest step into
  the card's activity log as they arrive; complete output lines are coalesced
  on a short timer so a chatty child does not rebuild the document per chunk.
- `TurnStatus` is the busy strip: elapsed timer, verb + target of the current
  tool ("Reading src/agentloop.cpp"), running sub-agents, completed tool count.

Keyboard shortcuts (panel-local, `QShortcut` on ChatWidget):

| Shortcut            | Action                          |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `Ctrl+Alt+E`        | Expand / collapse all tool cards |
| `Ctrl+Alt+Up/Down`  | Previous / next tool card       |
| `Ctrl+Alt+T`        | Expand / collapse thinking      |
| `Ctrl+Alt+P`        | Toggle plan mode (read-only)    |
| `Ctrl+Alt+Left/Right` | Previous / next model         |

## Tests

`tests/CMakeLists.txt` defines one QTest binary per component; core-level tests
need no GUI, widget tests add `../src/<widget>.cpp` and run `-platform offscreen`.
Some suites drive real subprocesses against `tests/mock_llm_server.py`,
`tests/mock_mcp_server.py` and `tests/mock_acp_agent.py`.

Build and run everything:

```sh
./build.sh          # cmake + build + ctest
```

Useful single suites:

- `test_tools` — every built-in tool, sandbox interaction, atomicity rules
- `test_sandbox` — path escapes, deny globs, command classification
- `test_modes` — mode parsing, tool groups, per-mode sampling overrides
- `test_projectgraph` — scan limits, binary detection, symlink loops, round-trip
- `test_livecards` / `test_toolcard` / `test_overflow` — widget-level behaviour
- `test_subtaskparallel` / `test_multiagent` — sub-agent concurrency and locks

## Persistence

- **Settings**: KConfig via `settings.cpp` (global, not per workspace).
- **Conversations**: SQLite through `SessionStore`; every turn autosaves, and the
  active conversation id is repaired to the newest transcript when stale.
- **Workspace state**: `.kateai/` — `KATEAI.md`, `modes/`, the MCP server
  config, and the cached `project_graph.json`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# macOS CI/local plugin build with KDE Craft (matching Kate ABI).
#
# There is no Homebrew ktexteditor formula, so a brew-only build cannot find
# KTextEditor (see scripts/kateai-platform.sh and install.sh, which point at
# Craft for the same reason). This script follows
# https://community.kde.org/Get_Involved/development/Mac :
#   1. Bootstrap Craft if missing (non-interactive, ~/CraftRoot).
#   2. `craft kate`              -> latest Kate + Qt/KF6 stack.
#   3. cmake build of this repo against ~/CraftRoot + ctest.
#   4. Stage artifacts/kateai.so.
#
# Usage: packaging/ci/macos-build.sh [--build-type Release] [--artifacts-dir artifacts]
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)"
cd "${ROOT}"

# GitHub macOS images export ANDROID_SDK_ROOT/ANDROID_NDK, which makes
# CraftBootstrap.isAndroid() true and produces an android-clang-arm64 ABI.
# KateAI does not build for Android: drop those markers for everything
# Craft-related in this script.
unset ANDROID_SDK_ROOT ANDROID_NDK

export HOMEBREW_NO_AUTO_UPDATE=1
# cmake/ninja are not guaranteed on the runner image (and nothing else
# installs them since the brew-deps approach was replaced by Craft).
# Idempotent: a no-op when already present.
for tool in cmake ninja git pkg-config; do
    command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || brew install "$tool"
done

BUILD_TYPE="Release"
ARTIFACTS="artifacts"
CRAFT_ROOT="${CRAFT_ROOT:-${HOME}/CraftRoot}"
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --build-type) BUILD_TYPE="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --artifacts-dir) ARTIFACTS="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --craft-root) CRAFT_ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        -h|--help) sed -n '1,12p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
        *) echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    esac
done

if [[ ! -f "${CRAFT_ROOT}/craft/craftenv.sh" ]]; then
    # Non-interactive: --use-defaults answers the setup wizard prompts
    # (target arch auto-detected, e.g. arm64 on Apple Silicon runners).
    echo "==> Bootstrapping KDE Craft into ${CRAFT_ROOT}"
    curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KDE/craft/master/setup/CraftBootstrap.py -o /tmp/CraftBootstrap.py
    python3 /tmp/CraftBootstrap.py --prefix "${CRAFT_ROOT}" --use-defaults
fi

echo "==> Loading Craft environment"
# craftenv.sh is not written with `set -u` in mind (unbound
# CRAFT_PYTHON_BIN aborts the source); relax nounset across the source.
set +u

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Mock OpenAI-compatible LLM used by the sub-agent parallel test.

The first request (the orchestrator) gets two new_task tool calls in a single
response. Requests whose last user message carries the CHILD marker are treated
as sub-agents and answered with plain text after a deliberate delay, so the test
can observe both sub-agents in flight at the same time. A request whose last
user message carries the QUESTION marker is answered with a single question tool
call, which the test must answer before the turn can finish.

Usage: mock_llm_server.py <port-file>
"""

import json
import os
import sys
import time
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer

CHILD_MARKER = "CHILD-TASK"
# What a question-flow test sends to make the mock ask something.
QUESTION_MARKER = "Ask the user something."
# Sent to make the mock ask a question with no text in it, which the loop must
# refuse rather than park the turn waiting for an answer to nothing.
EMPTY_QUESTION_MARKER = "Ask nothing at all."
# Sent to make the model post a suggestion with the suggest tool.
SUGGEST_MARKER = "Suggest an improvement."
# Same call, but the arguments arrive as a JSON object the way Ollama's
# OpenAI-compatible endpoint delivers them.
SUGGEST_OBJECT_ARGS_MARKER = "Suggest with object arguments."
# Sent to make the model run a long shell command, so a stop can be pressed
# while the command is still in flight.
STALL_MARKER = "Run a long command."
# The orchestrator's own prompt; only the first request looks like this.
PARENT_MARKER = "Split this across two agents."
# Sent to make the model write a file, so the pre-mutation checkpoint and the
# queued continuation can be observed.
WRITE_MARKER = "Write the note file."
# Sent to make the model stream text slowly, so a stop can be pressed while
# the answer is still being typed into the chat.
STREAM_MARKER = "Type slowly."
# Same, but the chunks are hidden reasoning: the stop has to freeze the
# paced reveal of thinking text, not only the visible answer.
THINK_MARKER = "Think slowly."
# Long enough that two sequential dispatches would visibly not overlap.
CHILD_DELAY_SECONDS = 1.5
# The orchestrator delegates exactly once; every later turn gets prose. Without
# this the parent would spawn sub-agents forever.
DELEGATED = False
# The question is asked once per server, for the same reason.
ASKED = False
ASKED_EMPTY = False
# The suggestion is posted once per server, for the same reason.
SUGGESTED = False
# The long command is issued once per server, for the same reason.
STALLED = False
# The file write is issued once per server, for the same reason.
WROTE = False
STREAMED = False
THOUGHT = False


def sse(payload):
    return f"data: {json.dumps(payload)}\n\n"


def chunk_text(text):
    return sse({"choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {"content": text}, "finish_reason": None}]})


def chunk_thinking(text):
    return sse({"choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {"reasoning_content": text}, "finish_reason": None}]})


def tool_call(index, call_id, name, arguments):
    return sse(
        {
            "choices": [
                {
                    "index": 0,
                    "delta": {
                        "tool_calls": [
                            {
                                "index": index,
                                "id": call_id,
                                "type": "function",
                                "function": {"name": name, "arguments": json.dumps(arguments)},
                            }
                        ]
                    },
                    "finish_reason": None,
                }
            ]
        }
    )


def tool_call_object_args(index, call_id, name, arguments):
    # Ollama and other local servers deliver the arguments as a JSON object
    # rather than a string. The client must cope with both shapes.
    return sse(
        {
            "choices": [
                {
                    "index": 0,
                    "delta": {
                        "tool_calls": [
                            {
                                "index": index,
                                "id": call_id,
                                "type": "function",
                                "function": {"name": name, "arguments": arguments},
                            }
                        ]
                    },
                    "finish_reason": None,
                }
            ]
        }
    )


class Handler(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def log_message(self, *args):  # keep the test output clean
        pass

    def do_POST(self):
        global DELEGATED, ASKED, ASKED_EMPTY, SUGGESTED, STALLED, WROTE, STREAMED, THOUGHT
        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length", "0"))
        try:
            body = json.loads(self.rfile.read(length) or b"{}")
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            self.send_error(400)
            return

        messages = body.get("messages", [])
        last_user = ""
        for message in messages:
            if message.get("role") == "user":
                content = message.get("content", "")
                if isinstance(content, list):
                    content = " ".join(
                        block.get("text", "") for block in content if isinstance(block, dict)
                    )
                last_user = content
        is_child = CHILD_MARKER in last_user
        is_orchestrator_first_turn = PARENT_MARKER in last_user and not DELEGATED
        is_question = QUESTION_MARKER in last_user and not ASKED
        is_empty_question = EMPTY_QUESTION_MARKER in last_user and not ASKED_EMPTY
        is_suggest = SUGGEST_MARKER in last_user and not SUGGESTED
        is_suggest_object_args = SUGGEST_OBJECT_ARGS_MARKER in last_user and not SUGGESTED
        is_write = WRITE_MARKER in last_user and not WROTE
        is_stream = STREAM_MARKER in last_user and not STREAMED
        is_think = THINK_MARKER in last_user and not THOUGHT
        # Anthropic puts the system prompt at the top level, so its requests are
        # the ones without a system-role message in the array.
        is_anthropic = "anthropic-version" in self.headers

        def respond(tool_name, call_id, arguments, object_args=False):
            if is_anthropic:
                # Messages API: tool arguments stream as JSON fragments after a
                # content_block_start that carries an empty input.
                emit(
                    "event: content_block_start\n"
                    + sse({"type": "content_block_start", "index": 0, "content_block": {"type": "tool_use", "id": call_id, "name": tool_name, "input": {}}})
                )
                emit(
                    "event: content_block_delta\n"
                    + sse(
                        {
                            "type": "content_block_delta",
                            "index": 0,
                            "delta": {"type": "input_json_delta", "partial_json": json.dumps(arguments)},
                        }
                    )
                )
                emit("event: message_delta\n" + sse({"type": "message_delta", "delta": {"stop_reason": "tool_use"}}))
                emit("event: message_stop\n" + sse({"type": "message_stop"}))
            else:
                emit(
                    tool_call_object_args(0, call_id, tool_name, arguments)
                    if object_args
                    else tool_call(0, call_id, tool_name, arguments)
                )
                emit(sse({"choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": "tool_calls"}]}))

        self.send_response(200)
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/event-stream")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.flush()

        def emit(text):
            self.wfile.write(text.encode())
            self.wfile.flush()

        if is_child:
            time.sleep(CHILD_DELAY_SECONDS)
            who = "A" if "agent-a" in last_user else "B"
            emit(chunk_text(f"[sub-agent {who}] finished its share of the work."))
            emit(sse({"choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}]}))
        elif STALL_MARKER in last_user and not STALLED:
            STALLED = True
            # A command long enough that the stop button can be pressed while
            # it is still running.
            respond("bash", "call_sleep", {"command": "sleep 30"})
        elif is_stream:
            STREAMED = True
            # Chunks spaced out over several seconds: a stop can be pressed
            # while the answer is visibly still streaming in.
            for i in range(30):
                emit(chunk_text(f"Streaming line {i} of the slow answer.\n\n"))
                time.sleep(0.2)
            emit(sse({"choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}]}))
        elif is_think:
            THOUGHT = True
            # Hidden reasoning, spaced out the same way: the stop has to
            # freeze the paced thinking reveal, not just the visible text.
            for i in range(20):
                emit(chunk_thinking(f"Thought {i} of the slow reasoning.\n\n"))
                time.sleep(0.25)
            emit(chunk_text("The reasoned answer."))
            emit(sse({"choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}]}))
        elif is_write:
            WROTE = True
            respond(
                "write_file",
                "call_write",
                {"path": "notes.txt", "content": "written by the mock model"},
            )
        elif is_orchestrator_first_turn:
            DELEGATED = True
            # Two independent subtasks in one response: these must overlap.
            emit(
                tool_call(
                    0,
                    "call_a",
                    "new_task",
                    {"description": f"{CHILD_MARKER} agent-a: handle the parser", "agent": "coder"},
                )
            )
            emit(
                tool_call(
                    1,
                    "call_b",
                    "new_task",
                    {"description": f"{CHILD_MARKER} agent-b: handle the writer", "agent": "coder"},
                )
            )
            emit(sse({"choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": "tool_calls"}]}))
        elif is_question:
            ASKED = True
            # One question with two offered answers: the turn cannot finish
            # until the user picks or types one.
            respond(
                "question",
                "call_q",
                {
                    "question": "Rewrite the file, or patch it in place?",
                    "options": ["Rewrite", "Patch"],
                },
            )
        elif is_empty_question:
            ASKED_EMPTY = True
            respond("question", "call_qe", {"question": ""})
        elif is_suggest_object_args:
            SUGGESTED = True
            respond(
                "suggest",
                "call_s",
                {
                    "suggestion": "Use std::string_view here instead of a const reference.",
                    "path": "src/main.cpp",
                    "line": 42,
                },
                object_args=True,
            )
        elif is_suggest:
            SUGGESTED = True
            # Advice the user never asked for: the suggestion tool is how the
            # agent raises it instead of editing the file itself.
            respond(
                "suggest",
                "call_s",
                {
                    "suggestion": "Use std::string_view here instead of a const reference.",
                    "path": "src/main.cpp",
                    "line": 42,
                },
            )
        else:
            # The orchestrator's follow-up turn: summarise in prose.
            emit(chunk_text("Both sub-agents reported back."))
            emit(sse({"choices": [{"index": 0, "delta": {}, "finish_reason": "stop"}]}))

        emit("data: [DONE]\n\n")


def main():
    server = ThreadingHTTPServer(("127.0.0.1", 0), Handler)
    server.daemon_threads = True
    if len(sys.argv) > 1:
        # Write the port atomically: create the file only once its contents are
        # fully flushed, so a test that waits for the file to appear never reads
        # a half-written (empty) port and parses it as 0.
        port_path = sys.argv[1]
        port_value = str(server.server_address[1])
        tmp_path = port_path + ".tmp"
        with open(tmp_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(port_value)
            handle.flush()
            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
        os.replace(tmp_path, port_path)
    server.serve_forever()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build the latest Kate editor from source and bundle it with this plugin.
#
# Result is a self-contained prefix:
#   <prefix>/bin/kate            # Kate built from KATE_REF (default: master)
#   <prefix>/lib/qt6/plugins/kf6/ktexteditor/kateai.so
#   <prefix>/bin/kate-ai         # wrapper that launches the bundled Kate
# plus a tarball in packaging/dist/ for CI releases.
#
# Usage:
#   packaging/bundle-kate.sh [--kate-ref master] [--prefix /opt/kate-ai-bundle]
#                            [--out packaging/dist/kate-bundle-<ver>.tar.gz]
#                            [--kate-dir <existing-checkout>] [--skip-kate]
#
# --skip-kate reuses an already-built prefix (only rebuilds the plugin).
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "${ROOT}"
# shellcheck source=scripts/kateai-platform.sh
source "${ROOT}/scripts/kateai-platform.sh"

KATE_GIT_URL="${KATE_GIT_URL:-https://invent.kde.org/utilities/kate.git}"
KATE_REF="${KATE_REF:-master}"
PREFIX="/opt/kate-ai-bundle"
OUT=""
KATE_DIR=""
SKIP_KATE=0
BUILD_TYPE="RelWithDebInfo"
JOBS="$(kateai_jobs)"

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --kate-ref) KATE_REF="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --prefix) PREFIX="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --out) OUT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --kate-dir) KATE_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --skip-kate) SKIP_KATE=1; shift ;;
        --release) BUILD_TYPE="Release"; shift ;;
        --debug) BUILD_TYPE="Debug"; shift ;;
        -h|--help)
            sed -n '1,20p' "$0"
            exit 0
            ;;
        *) echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    esac
done

VERSION="$(sed -n 's/^project(kateai VERSION \([^ ]*\).*/\1/p' "${ROOT}/CMakeLists.txt" | head -1)"
VERSION="${VERSION:-0.1.0}"
KATE_SHORT="$(echo "${KATE_REF}" | tr '/ ' '__')"
if [[ -z "${OUT}" ]]; then
    OUT="${ROOT}/packaging/dist/kate-bundle-${VERSION}-kate-${KATE_SHORT}-$(uname -m).tar.gz"
fi

WORKDIR="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "${WORKDIR}"' EXIT

if [[ "${SKIP_KATE}" -eq 0 ]]; then
    if [[ -z "${KATE_DIR}" ]]; then
        KATE_DIR="${WORKDIR}/kate"
        echo "==> Cloning Kate (${KATE_REF}) from ${KATE_GIT_URL}"
        git clone --depth 1 --branch "${KATE_REF}" "${KATE_GIT_URL}" "${KATE_DIR}" 2>/dev/null \
        || git clone --depth 1 "${KATE_GIT_URL}" "${KATE_DIR}"
        if [[ "${KATE_REF}" != "master" ]]; then
            (cd "${KATE_DIR}" && git fetch --depth 1 origin "${KATE_REF}" 2>/dev/null && git checkout FETCH_HEAD) || true
        fi
    fi
    echo "==> Building Kate (${KATE_REF}) into ${PREFIX}"
    cmake -S "${KATE_DIR}" -B "${WORKDIR}/build-kate" \
        -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE="${BUILD_TYPE}" \
        -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="${PREFIX}" \
        -DBUILD_TESTING=OFF \
        -G Ninja
    cmake --build "${WORKDIR}/build-kate" -j"${JOBS}"
    if [[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]]; then
        cmake --install "${WORKDIR}/build-kate"
    else
        sudo cmake --install "${WORKDIR}/build-kate" 2>/dev/null \
        || cmake --install "${WORKDIR}/build-kate" --prefix "${PREFIX}"
    fi
else
    echo "==> Reusing existing Kate prefix at ${PREFIX}"
fi

echo "==> Building Kate AI plugin against ${PREFIX}"
# USE_QT_SYS_PATHS=OFF: the plugin must land under the bundle prefix.
# ON would resolve the *system* Qt plugin dir (/usr/lib64/...) and the
# bundle check below would fail on exactly that installed-to-system file.
cmake -S "${ROOT}" -B "${WORKDIR}/build-kateai" \
    -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE="${BUILD_TYPE}" \
    -DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX="${PREFIX}" \
    -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="${PREFIX}" \
    -DKATEAI_USER_INSTALL=OFF \
    -DKDE_INSTALL_USE_QT_SYS_PATHS=OFF \
    -DBUILD_TESTING=OFF \
    -G Ninja
cmake --build "${WORKDIR}/build-kateai" -j"${JOBS}"
if [[ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]]; then
    DESTDIR="" cmake --install "${WORKDIR}/build-kateai"
else
    sudo cmake --install "${WORKDIR}/build-kateai" 2>/dev/null \
    || (echo "sudo failed, installing with user permissions into ${PREFIX}" >&2; cmake --install "${WORKDIR}/build-kateai")
fi

PLUGIN_SO="$(find "${PREFIX}" -path '*kf6/ktexteditor/kateai.so' 2>/dev/null | head -1 || true)"
if [[ -z "${PLUGIN_SO}" ]]; then
    echo "Bundle failed: kateai.so not found under ${PREFIX}" >&2
    exit 1
fi
echo "Bundled plugin: ${PLUGIN_SO}"
ls -l "${PLUGIN_SO}"

# Wrapper so the bundle runs without env setup: the plugin already lives in
# the prefix's Qt plugin dir, so plain `kate` is enough. The plugin dir is
# derived from where the .so actually landed (lib vs lib64 varies per
# distro) and stored relative to the prefix, so the tarball stays
# relocatable instead of hard-coding /opt or lib/.
PLUGIN_BASE="$(dirname "$(dirname "$(dirname "${PLUGIN_SO}")")")"
PLUGIN_RELPATH="$(realpath --relative-to="${PREFIX}" "${PLUGIN_BASE}")"
cat > "${PREFIX}/bin/kate-ai" <<EOF
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
HERE="\$(cd "\$(dirname "\$0")" && pwd)"
PREFIX="\$(cd "\${HERE}/.." && pwd)"
export QT_PLUGIN_PATH="\${PREFIX}/${PLUGIN_RELPATH}\${QT_PLUGIN_PATH:+:\$QT_PLUGIN_PATH}"
exec "\${PREFIX}/bin/kate" "\$@"
EOF
chmod +x "${PREFIX}/bin/kate-ai"

mkdir -p "$(dirname "${OUT}")"
echo "==> Packing ${PREFIX} -> ${OUT}"
tar -C "$(dirname "${PREFIX}")" -czf "${OUT}" "$(basename "${PREFIX}")"
ls -l "${OUT}"
echo "Bundle ready: ${OUT}"
echo "Run it: tar -xzf ${OUT} -C / && /opt/kate-ai-bundle/bin/kate-ai"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Bundle the latest Kate (built via Craft) with this plugin on macOS.
#
# Result in packaging/dist/:
#   kate-<ver>-macos-<arch>.dmg      # latest Kate installer built by Craft
#   kateai-<ver>-macos-<arch>.zip    # this plugin (Craft/Clang ABI)
#
# Install: open the .dmg to install Kate, then run ./install.sh (it copies
# kateai.so into Kate.app and sets up the LaunchAgent).
#
# Usage: packaging/bundle-kate-macos.sh [--out-dir packaging/dist] [--skip-kate]
set -euo pipefail
ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/.." && pwd)"
cd "${ROOT}"
# GitHub macOS images export ANDROID_SDK_ROOT/ANDROID_NDK, which makes
# CraftBootstrap.isAndroid() true and produces an android-clang-arm64 ABI.
# KateAI does not build for Android: drop those markers for everything
# Craft-related in this script (also inherited by macos-build.sh below).
unset ANDROID_SDK_ROOT ANDROID_NDK
# shellcheck source=scripts/kateai-platform.sh
source "${ROOT}/scripts/kateai-platform.sh"

CRAFT_ROOT="${CRAFT_ROOT:-${HOME}/CraftRoot}"
OUT_DIR="${ROOT}/packaging/dist"
SKIP_KATE=0
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --out-dir) OUT_DIR="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        --skip-kate) SKIP_KATE=1; shift ;;
        --craft-root) CRAFT_ROOT="$2"; shift 2 ;;
        -h|--help) sed -n '1,12p' "$0"; exit 0 ;;
        *) echo "Unknown option: $1" >&2; exit 1 ;;
    esac
done

VERSION="$(sed -n 's/^project(kateai VERSION \([^ ]*\).*/\1/p' "${ROOT}/CMakeLists.txt" | head -1)"
VERSION="${VERSION:-0.1.0}"
ARCH="$(uname -m)"

if [[ ! -f "${CRAFT_ROOT}/craft/craftenv.sh" ]]; then
    # Non-interactive: --use-defaults answers the setup wizard prompts.
    echo "==> Bootstrapping KDE Craft into ${CRAFT_ROOT}"
    curl https://raw.githubusercontent.com/KDE/craft/master/setup/CraftBootstrap.py -o /tmp/CraftBootstrap.py
    python3 /tmp/CraftBootstrap.py --prefix "${CRAFT_ROOT}" --use-defaults
fi
if [[ ! -f "${CRAFT_ROOT}/craft/craftenv.sh" ]]; then
    echo "KDE Craft bootstrap failed for ${CRAFT_ROOT}." >&2
    echo "See https://community.kde.org/Get_Involved/development/Mac" >&2
    exit 1
fi
echo "==> Loading Craft environment"
# craftenv.sh is not written with `set -u` in mind (unbound
# CRAFT_PYTHON_BIN aborts the source); relax nounset across the source.
set +u
# shellcheck source=/dev/null
source "${CRAFT_ROOT}/craft/craftenv.sh"
set -u

if [[ "${SKIP_KATE}" -eq 0 ]]; then
    echo "==> Building latest Kate via Craft"
    craft kate
fi

echo "==> Building plugin against ${CRAFT_ROOT}"
/usr/bin/env bash "${ROOT}/packaging/ci/macos-build.sh" --build-type Release --artifacts-dir "${ROOT}/artifacts-macos-tmp"

echo "==> Packaging Kate installer (.dmg) via Craft"
craft --package kate

mkdir -p "${OUT_DIR}"
DMG="$(find "${CRAFT_ROOT}/tmp" -maxdepth 1 -name 'kate-*.dmg' -print 2>/dev/null | sort | tail -1 || true)"
if [[ -n "${DMG}" && -f "${DMG}" ]]; then
    cp -f "${DMG}" "${OUT_DIR}/kate-${VERSION}-macos-${ARCH}.dmg"
else
    echo "WARNING: no kate-*.dmg found under ${CRAFT_ROOT}/tmp; shipping plugin only." >&2
fi
rm -f "${OUT_DIR}/kateai-${VERSION}-macos-${ARCH}.zip"
(cd "${ROOT}/artifacts-macos-tmp" && zip -j "${OUT_DIR}/kateai-${VERSION}-macos-${ARCH}.zip" kateai.so)
rm -rf "${ROOT}/artifacts-macos-tmp"
ls -l "${OUT_DIR}"/kate-*-macos-*.dmg "${OUT_DIR}"/kateai-*-macos-*.zip 2>/dev/null || true
echo "Bundle ready in ${OUT_DIR}"

# Absolute path to python3, resolved at configure time so tests can spawn it
# even when PATH is rewritten (Craft's craftenv.sh on macOS/Windows CI).
if(Python3_Interpreter_FOUND)
    # Escape backslashes so a Windows path survives the C++ string literal
    # (raw backslashes would be misread as escape sequences).
    set(KATEAI_PYTHON3 "${Python3_EXECUTABLE}")
    string(REPLACE "\\" "\\\\" KATEAI_PYTHON3 "${KATEAI_PYTHON3}")
    add_compile_definitions(KATEAI_PYTHON3="${KATEAI_PYTHON3}")
endif()
